- Contrary to a claim circulating via social media posts, there's no evidence that House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries explicitly threatened to withhold committee assignments from House members and members-elect who don't support his bid for speaker when Democrats take control of the legislative body in January.
- This rumor stemmed from Ohio Democratic Rep.-elect Don Leonard's comments about a dinner with senior Democratic representatives who allegedly warned Leonard that his life could become a "living hell" if he didn't support Jeffries. Leonard later told TMZ that potential consequences could include withheld committee assignments, but he framed it as a possibility as to what that "living hell" may entail.
- Snopes will update this report if we receive replies to our queries from either Leonard or Jeffries.
After Democrats won control of Congress in the 2026 midterms, a claim spread online that U.S. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries was threatening to withhold committee assignments for any of his caucus members who didn't support him for speaker of the House.
The rumor circulated on X and Threads, and Snopes readers wrote in to ask us to verify it.
This claim originated from Ohio Democratic Rep.-elect Don Leonard's comments about "friendly advice with very stark consequences" he allegedly received from senior House Democrats in regard to supporting Jeffries' bid for speaker. Social media posts appear to have taken Leonard's comments somewhat out of context. There's no evidence that Jeffries has literally threatened to withhold committee assignments from anyone who does not support him as speaker.
Jeffries and Leonard's offices did not immediately return requests for more information. Here's what we know:
Leonard's allegations
Leonard, an Ohio Democrat who flipped a Republican-held seat, posted a video on Nov. 9 claiming that top House Democrats said his life will become a "living hell" if he doesn't support Jeffries. 
Leonard says in the video that he will not support Jeffries as speaker without the New York Democrat's commitments to two issues: ending U.S. support for Israeli military actions, including the war in Iran, and a constitutional amendment that would reverse Citizens United, a Supreme Court decision that gives free-speech protections to corporate money in politics.
Here's the transcript from that video (emphasis ours):
Tonight, I met with — we'll call 'em senior members of the Democratic House — who told me in no uncertain terms that the decision as to whether or not I support Jeffries, regardless of his willingness to speak with me and meet the interests of my constituents on a couple of key issues: No. 1, getting a constitutional amendment to end Citizens United, and No. 2, ending U.S. support for the war in Iran, and the country, Israel, that led us into it — that that would basically mean both making my life a living hell for the next two years in Washington as well as being sure to lose my election in two years.
You know, we kinda knew this stuff was coming. It's part of the stuff you see in the movies. It's a whole 'nother thing when, you know, it's in person by people who actually care about you and are cheering for you, but expect you to wear the team jersey and, you know, be a good team player. You know, we're searching our hearts tonight as to how we can reach Leader Jeffries and help him be a better speaker. At the end of the day, the big "D" Democratic Party needs some little "d" democracy and I'm just a stubborn SOB, so we'll continue meeting with our fellow members of Congress and members-elect and try and see if we can build support for what we're trying to do here. Please wish me luck. It's getting real, y'all.
On Nov. 11, TMZ posted a video in which a reporter with the tabloid asks Leonard about his comments. In that video, Leonard expands on what "living hell" could mean and says committee assignments could be withheld. However, he also makes it clear that the conversation he was referencing did not directly involve Jeffries, nor was it meant to be threatening.
As such, it's unclear whether anyone actually told Leonard that Jeffries would withhold committee assignments from him or any other Democrat who does not support Jeffries as speaker.
Here's a transcript of the TMZ interview (emphasis ours):
TMZ: You're in a room with top-level Dem officials. They say to you, "Listen, if you don't fall in line, we're going to make your life hell." Walk me through what that experience was like, just on your first couple of days here.
LEONARD: It was so much less cinematic. It was actually a dinner with senior elected officials, and I let them know where my position was on the speaker, and they were offering very friendly advice with very stark consequences. It wasn't in leadership, it wasn't their position to do it. It was just, you know, friendly advice from future colleagues.
TMZ: It doesn't sound that friendly. You literally said — your words — you said it was out of a movie. It sounds like something out of like "The Godfather."
LEONARD: What's out of a movie is the consequences of it, right? And the consequences are very real. Committee assignments will be withheld. You know, The ability to get, you know, legislation on the floor for votes will be difficult. And, you know, the ability to get support for the re-election will be a difficult case to make.
TMZ: Is this not what people criticize Trump for? It sounds very similar.
LEONARD: Yeah, I know, I think, you know, well, welcome to Washington, D.C., right? I mean, it's — I'm not shocked, but I'm —
TMZ: Sounds a little shocking. I think you're a little —
LEONARD: — I'm disappointed.
TMZ: Yeah, well listen. We can say — you already said what you had to say. And it's gone viral. But I think we gotta go the next step further, here, just for Americans. Who were these people who said it to you?
LEONARD: Yeah, no, that's how we build relationships and sustain them going forward. But I appreciate it.
TMZ: You don't want to get in trouble, hey man, I appreciate it.
Axios reportedly asked Leonard about the conversation, per a Nov. 11 story, and he emphasized that it was a "friendly" and "well-intentioned" conversation with senior House Democrats. Here's how he described it to Axios:
"They let me know that while we all agree on a lot of this stuff … the leader is going to pursue his message and agenda as he sees fit, and [said], 'Don't be insane. How could you possibly stand in the way?'"
Leonard also said he met Jeffries for the first time, per Axios, and there's no indication it was a threatening meeting:
The Ohio Democrat said he got a chance to meet Jeffries for the first time on Tuesday and arrange for their staffers to work out a time to sit down and talk.
- "I shook his hand and I asked him for six minutes," he said, telling Axios he wants to "look him in the eye, let him know that [I] respect his capacity as a leader ... but I need something to take back to my district that shows that my party understands the magnitude of the crisis we face."
Politico reported that California Democrat Rep. Pete Aguilar, who is running unopposed for House majority whip, said he didn't know which Democrats Leonard was referring to.
"It's my belief that he will be overwhelmingly selected to lead this caucus. I don't lose any sleep over that," Aguilar reportedly said of Jeffries. "Members could have ideas and interests, and they could have asks along the way, but the outcome is not in question."
It's also worth noting that Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota, an outspoken progressive, told TMZ that no one has threatened her over Jeffries' bid for speaker. Omar suggested that Leonard simply received "advice that seems intimidating" and said Congress was "like high school: If people see any weakness, they'll roll with it, they'll take advantage of you."

Where does Kane rank among all-time England greats?
- Published
Harry Kane is now England's most-capped men's player as well as his country's record goalscorer, but harder to quantify is where these achievements place him among the Three Lions' greatest ever players.
This is a tricky debate with so many variables and a timescale as old as the game itself and, to my mind, not merely a determination of a player's individual ability but also a measure of their impact upon the nation's psyche.
Ballon d'Or winners Stanley Matthews, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen would surely have a shout if the criteria was such, not to mention genius technicians such as Glenn Hoddle, Chris Waddle and John Barnes.
Likewise, if any England boss managed to extract the best from Paul Scholes, Steven Gerrard and Frank Lampard they would be surely making a classic late dart from midfield.
But to qualify as one of the greatest England players of all time, you need the above ability combined with an impactful overall contribution - those memorable moments and an element of longevity - in a Three Lions shirt.
It might be controversial then to leave out Geoff Hurst, who produced the most recognisable performance in England history, while the man he replaced, Jimmy Greaves, would be a shoo-in were it not for injury earlier in the tournament.
It is also hard to rank the contribution of those whose best football came outside of major tournaments and before the dawn of continental competitions - see Eddie Hapgood, Tom Finney, Nat Lofthouse, Dixie Dean et al.
There are only 10 spots, after all, so here we go.
10. David Beckham
Spice Boy. Celebrity. Galactico. There is no argument David Beckham is one of the most iconic England players of all time, but he backed it up on the pitch, too.
Beckham was the face of the Three Lions for a generation, and to his credit managed to overcome the vicious fallout of his red card against Argentina in 1998.
At times he seemed to single-handedly carry England, most notably scoring a 93rd-minute free-kick against Greece to qualify for the 2002 World Cup.
Beckham's former team-mate Gary Neville called him the "most influential player out of England in transforming football".
It's true. On top of 115 caps, Beckham was part of Manchester United's 1999 Treble-winning outfit - finishing Ballon d'Or runner-up - before joining Real Madrid.
His profile was truly global with spells at LA Galaxy, AC Milan and Paris St-Germain.
9. Paul Gascoigne
There's arguably no England star fans forged an emotional attachment with more than Gazza - crying with him in 1990, rejoicing in his spectacular effort against Scotland and desperately willing him to connect during that Euro 96 semi-final defeat by Germany.
Gascoigne won 57 caps and scored 10 goals. At his peak, he was captivating - transcending football as a cultural phenomenon during the summers of '90 and '96, having joined a star-studded Serie A between those tournaments.
Creative, unpredictable, vulnerable. He was a loveable but flawed genius.
He suffered long-term injuries as England missed out on Euro 92 and the World Cup in the USA, but helped the Three Lions qualify for France 98 before being dropped from the final squad, famously wrecking boss Glenn Hoddle's office.
8. Billy Wright
Goalscorers often grab the headlines but I've tried to credit players across positions and eras. From a defensive point of view Ashley Cole, arguably England's best-ever full-back, was close to making it.
But instead it's the great Billy Wright, the first men's player to surpass a century of international caps, including a remarkable 70 successive appearances over eight years.
Wright captained his country on 90 occasions, a joint-record recently broken by Kane, taking in three World Cups with impressive longevity for his era.
He was a true one-club man, winning three league titles, the FA Cup and becoming unofficial "world champions" with Wolves in 1954 - helping inspire the birth of the European Cup - while finishing Ballon d'Or runner-up to Alfredo di Stefano in 1957.
7. Jude Bellingham
It feels a little premature to include a 23-year-old with the bulk of his England career ahead of him, but that shows the impact Jude Bellingham has already made for England and Real Madrid.
A Champions League winner, the midfielder has also appeared at four major tournaments for the Three Lions, becoming the youngest player to do so at the delayed Euro 2020, aged 17.
But his role in helping carry England to the final two years ago and a third-place finish at last summer's World Cup really make him stand out.
Bellingham has delivered those moments a nation collectively remembers. The last-gasp overhead kick against Slovakia in 2024, a quickfire double at the Azteca against Mexico this summer and 93rd-minute quarter-final winner against Norway.
His seven goals at this World Cup were more than any previous Three Lions player in a single edition, the solo effort against France a thing of beauty.
The former Birmingham and Dortmund man doesn't turn 24 until June but has already collected 61 England caps and netted 14 times. As Roy Keane put it, Bellingham has the potential to be one of the "greatest of all time".
6. Wayne Rooney
In terms of natural ability, Wayne Rooney is among England's greatest ever talents.
Bursting on to the scene at Euro 2004 as an electric 18-year-old, having become England's youngest player and scorer the previous year, convinced fans and media the teen sensation could carry the Three Lions to glory in Portugal.
He bounced World Cup winner Lilian Thuram around in England's opener against France in a glimpse of his precocious strength, before scoring twice against both Switzerland and Croatia.
Who knows how far England would have gone had Rooney not been injured against Portugal in the quarter-final?
He was unable to replicate the impact of his first Euros - a red card at World Cup 2006, suspension for the Euro 2012 group stage, seven goals across six major tournaments - but was an all-rounder who brought more than just goals.
Rooney also won it all with Manchester United, becoming the club's all-time top scorer, and finished his 15-year England career with 53 goals from 120 caps.
5. Gordon Banks
There has to be a place for a goalkeeper, and Gordon Banks is the safest pair of hands.
A World Cup winner in 1966, his save from Pele four years later against Brazil is one of the most iconic of all time. Pele called him a "goalkeeper with magic".
Banks spent the majority of his career at Leicester and Stoke, winning a League Cup with each, and earned 73 England caps overall between 1963 and 1972.
His incredible athleticism and reflexes saw the shot-stopper named Fifa's best goalkeeper for five successive years between 1966 and 1971.
4. Gary Lineker
Gary Lineker's early club career did not deliver the silverware as his goals deserved, netting 40 times but finishing league and FA Cup runner-up in his one season at Everton before joining Barcelona.
He scored a Clasico hat-trick and won the Copa del Rey and Cup Winner's Cup, however, before adding an FA Cup with Tottenham in 1991.
Lineker netted 283 club goals (and famously no cards) in total across spells with Leicester, Everton, Barcelona, Spurs and Nagoya Grampus Eight.
But as a player Lineker is most renowned for his contribution in an England shirt, winning the Golden Boot as they reached the World Cup quarter-finals in 1986 - finishing Ballon d'Or runner-up that year - before netting another four as the Three Lions reached the semi-finals in 1990.
Lineker equalised against West Germany before England crashed out on penalties.
However, having missed a spot-kick against Brazil, he finished one short of Bobby Charlton's elusive goal record when his international career ended after Euro 92.
3. Harry Kane
Harry Kane is undoubtedly England's most important and influential player of a generation - it is hard to imagine how this Three Lions side functions once the skipper hangs up his boots.
The Bayern Munich striker, complete with Ballon d'Or, has been scoring goals for his country for almost 12 years, the first just 79 seconds into his debut after coming off the bench against Lithuania in March 2015.
Rooney's goalscoring benchmark is long in his rear view mirror - you wouldn't bank against Kane doubling his nearest rival's figure once his England days are over.
They have come on the biggest stage, too - 21 in 36 appearances from three World Cups and European Championships apiece, winning the World Cup Golden Boot in 2018.
Kane has come closer to winning a major tournament than any England men's captain since Bobby Moore - losing two World Cup semi-finals and back-to-back Euros finals. Team-mate Bellingham called him the "greatest player that has ever played for England".
"I think we'll appreciate him even more in another 10, 15, 20 years when you look back and see what he has achieved," said ex-England goalkeeper Paul Robinson.
2. Bobby Moore
In many ways, Bobby Moore would be the complete modern-day defender. Cool as you like under pressure, elegant in possession, a great passing range off both feet and, as his West Ham and England team-mate Geoff Hurst said: "Nobody out-ran him and nobody out-jumped him."
Moore's positioning and timing was perfect, that iconic tackle on Jairzinho at the 1970 World Cup the finest example of his poise and precision when defending.
He was also a composed and influential leader. A player built for the big occasions. England boss Sir Alf Ramsey called him: "My lieutenant on the field, a cool, calculated footballer I could trust with my life."
The Barking-born centre-back won the FA Cup and European Cup Winners' Cup with West Ham but his finest moment was leading England to glory in 1966. He was only 25 at the time, having become his country's youngest captain three years earlier.
In 1970, after the Bogota bracelet incident, Moore was imperious as England reached the quarter-finals before bowing out to West Germany.
It was, however, the final group game against Brazil, the most exciting side on the planet, that produced some of the most recognisable and renowned images in sporting history - not only Moore's tackle and Banks' save but the defender swapping shirts with Pele after the final whistle.
"The greatest defender I ever played against," was the Brazilian's verdict.
1. Sir Bobby Charlton
For more than a generation, Sir Bobby's England goalscoring record remained unmatched. It took 55 years from his 49th and final strike against Colombia in 1970 until Rooney surpassed him with his half century in 2015.
Charlton was, as Alan Shearer put it, "not only a great goalscorer but a scorer of great goals" and played a pivotal part of the Three Lions' World Cup success in 1966, netting three times on the way to the final.
A scampering run from the halfway line followed by a trademark long-range strike into the corner at Wembley gave England's campaign lift-off against Mexico, before he scored twice against Eusebio's Portugal in the semi-finals.
Manager Ramsey called the buccaneering midfielder his "lynchpin" as England triumphed over West Germany in the showpiece and those performances helped Charlton win the Ballon d'Or later that year.
He'd be runner-up in successive years after that, too.
Charlton won 106 England caps and was a star for Manchester United, with Rooney also the one to pip his club-record 249 goals for the Old Trafford outfit.
A survivor of the Munich air disaster on 6 February 1958, which killed 23 people including eight players and three members of the club's staff, Charlton won three league titles, an FA Cup and most poignantly the European Cup in 1968.
"England's greatest ever player," Lineker previously told BBC Radio 5 Live.
"He was unique. Wherever you go in the world, even if they didn't speak the language, they knew two words - Bobby Charlton."

A rumor that U.S. President Donald Trump wrote a social media post chastising Vice President JD Vance, including an order to change the vice president's name, circulated in November.
People on social media shared a purported screenshot of a social media post attributed to Trump that claimed, "I'm hereby signing an EXCLUSIVE ORDER legally changing JD Vance's name to JUDAS DISLOYAL VANCE!"
(X user @miribobs)
The alleged post was dated Nov. 5 and inspired readers to reach out about its authenticity. It circulated after Democrats enjoyed major victories in the 2026 U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3.
It read in full:
I'm hereby signing an EXCLUSIVE ORDER legally changing JD Vance's name to JUDAS DISLOYAL VANCE!
Nobody gave JD more than President Trump. I took him from the sidelines and gave him the biggest job of his life—and now he thinks he can DOUBLE CROSS THE BOSS and run for President in 2028 without my blessing?
EHHH!
WRONG!
You don't walk into the Trump Family, eat at the table, kiss the ring, and then decide you're the new Boss!
There is only ONE person who can make America Great Again the RIGHT WAY, and everybody knows who that is.
JD, you may have forgotten who made you—but I NEVER forget!
THE PRESIDENT HAS SPOKEN.
The post was fake, however.
A search of the president's Truth Social account and an online archive of his social media posts revealed no such post.
The fake Trump post circulated as an apparent response, likely satirical, to a Nov. 4 X post by Vance addressing the Republican turnout at the polls for the midterm elections. Vance wrote: "The main problem is not turnout. The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026." His post sparked rumors that he's angling for a 2028 bid for the White House.
The engagement metrics displayed on the fake post — 14.3K reposts, 56.7K likes — exactly match those of other debunked Trump posts, suggesting it may have been generated using a template or a fake post generator. Note that the timestamp is written out as "11/5/26," while authentic Truth Social posts show dates written as "Nov 5, 2026."
The president made multiple posts on Truth Social on that date, but nothing about Vance or a rumored bid for the White House.

‘Tackling inequality is key for India in age of change’: Economist Joseph E Stiglitz at HT Leadership Summit
He also warned that climate impacts will hit tropical regions hard and said national economic sovereignty may increasingly shape global policy.
The US in the twilight of its power and China needing to reorient its economy away from exports to domestic consumption are the central contradictions facing today’s global economy, economist and Nobel laureate Joseph Stiglitz said at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit on Saturday.
The new world order will be multipolar unlike the unipolar US-dominated world order that existed after the second world war. Adjusting to it will not be easy for all countries. India’s key opportunity and challenge lies in managing its domestic inequality; and if done well, there is no reason the nation cannot sustain high levels of growth, the US economist said.
What the world needs to navigate this phase is the leadership of young, idealistic and pragmatic people. It also needs the rest of the world, especially the so-called middle powers, to stand up together against bully-like behaviour from the US, which is what it has become under President Donald Trump, he added. The former is what seems to have worked for the Democratic Party in the recent mid-term elections in the US, Stiglitz said, while adding that he worries about the rise of right-wing politics among men under 35 even as women continue to support progressive politics in the US.
Deep Dive
The biggest change in the global economic order came in the last decade when China overtook US’s GDP in purchasing power parity (PPP) terms, Stiglitz pointed out. But neither of them advertised it in a big way as the US could not accept losing its leadership and China was still interested in exploiting the export route to growth. With China reaching an unprecedented trade surplus of more than a trillion dollars, the global economic balance is untenable now. There is no way the rest of the world can accommodate China’s large trade surplus and the latter needs to reorient its economy towards domestic consumption, and a better quality of life, he added.
Also Read | AI bubble will break; India should be worried: Economist Joseph E Stiglitz at HT Leadership Summit 2026
China’s economic rise as an export superpower worked well for Americans initially. “It wasn’t (Alan) Greenspan, it was China that kept our prices down. So, we should say thank you to China…But China has grown so much over the last 30 years…Nobody had a sense that it would become a competitor to the United States, the competitor that it has become,” Stiglitz said.
The US economy has also seen a larger increase in the monopoly power of companies and an arrangement where the super-rich do not pay their fair share of taxes, he said.
The latter is the biggest reason why the US is staring at a fiscal cliff in terms of extremely high deficit and debt burden today, he added. Unlike during the Second World War, there is no other reason to justify the high deficit and debt levels in today’s US, he contended. Growing debt levels in the advanced economies, especially the US, unless corrected by taxing the super-rich, will raise the cost of capital for all nations, including India, he added.
Inequality is a problem, not just within countries, but also between countries, Stiglitz explained.
Migration pressures in advanced economies in both the US and Europe, which are linked to global inequality, are generating a lot of anxieties.
Politicians like Trump are a product of that, Stiglitz said. In the name of addressing these anxieties, Trump is undoing the biggest advantage the US enjoyed in the past.
“The United States really did have some strengths. We attracted the best people from all over the world to our universities, and many of them stayed there. You look at Silicon Valley, half of them are Indians. And so we were the place that benefited from the talents of the entire world. And now under Donald Trump, he’s attacked our universities, he’s attacked our research, he’s defunded our science,” Sitglitz said.
Also Read | Economist Joseph Stiglitz on how China makes entire global economy unstable | HTLS 2026
“The world needs a better understanding of inequality and this is why I have been arguing for a global panel on inequality on the lines of what we did on the issue of climate change,” he explained. It needs to be treated as a systemic political economic risk, he added.
Stiglitz was member of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) in the 1990s.
Climate change has happened at a much faster pace than what IPCC had assumed then, the economist said. While this acceleration will adversely affect every part of the world, tropical areas, India included, will be particularly severely hit, he added. “I have heard that ground water sustainability is becoming a crisis in India. If this is allowed to reach a situation where agricultural productivity comes down, the consequences will be very serious.”
The resurrection of borders mattering again in today’s world is not just on account of Trump but a more widespread phenomenon, he added. “National economic sovereignty” will be a defining feature of the global economic order going forward and this could even entail capital controls, not just tariffs,” Stiglitz added.
Also Read | HT Leadership Summit: Economist Joseph E Stiglitz questions value of trade deals with Trump’s US
“What worries me, both in India and the United States, is the balance between demand and supply. If you have a country with growing inequality, like the United States, you won’t have the demand…Now the big advantage that India has is it has a huge domestic market, if you manage it well…if you make sure that income inequality is not too great then I think there is enough domestic demand and enough room to grow, because you’re still so much below the global frontier that I think there’s no reason why you can’t continue to grow at 7%”, he said.
India also needs to make sure that it continues to invest in both human capital, especially education and keeps adding to its physical infrastructure. India will also need to maintain fiscal discipline going forward, he added. The latter is especially relevant given the fact that return on investment in advanced countries, particularly the US, is going to become higher, he said.

I left the classroom a couple of years ago. I told myself it was for good, but my husband made me promise him that I was really done. In return, I asked him not to let me go back if I ever tried to again.
Deep down, I can still sense my love of teaching, and since my husband knows me well, these are promises I know we'll both keep.
I knew my professional teaching certificate was going to expire this summer, and I went back and forth about whether or not I should go to the trouble of renewing it. In an extreme act of setting boundaries, I decided to let it go — on purpose. I was worried I would regret it, but now I'm glad I let it expire.
I felt a huge sigh of relief when my teaching certificate was no longer active
I had no realistic intentions of returning to the classroom, but it was difficult to think about how much work I had put into obtaining my professional teaching certificate. But every time I considered going through the steps to keep my license up to date, it didn't make sense.
I have no intention of teaching again, so spending my time and money to keep my license felt like holding onto something that wasn't right for me anymore.
My push out of the classroom came unwillingly, as my health was deteriorating, making it increasingly difficult for me to do my job. I even took a few months off toward the end to focus on my health before returning to the classroom, but it ended up the same way. As soon as I went back to work, my symptoms flared back up, and I couldn't finish the school year again.
I had to accept that I couldn't physically do my job
Shortly after I left teaching for good, I finally got my endometriosis diagnosis. I had an answer as to why I had been getting increasingly sick over the last five years. Unfortunately, I didn't receive care before the disease changed my career route. The majority of my time now is spent managing my symptoms and doing my best to regain a lot of physical function after two major surgeries in the last two years.
I thought I was content with my decision, but then one of my friends mentioned she was taking a recertification course to meet her own career licensing requirements. I doubted my decision for a moment. I even consulted some old Reddit posts to see what other people in my position had done and if they regretted letting their own certificates expire. The advice seemed to be a mixed bag.
I had to remind myself why I was making this decision
I wanted that temptation removed. I needed to keep myself from moving backward so I could figure out what's next. In a very real way, I am still grieving my old self, before my endometriosis progressed. I miss being able to do something like teach all day, and every time I miss it, I have to deal with remembering why I had to give it up.
More on making a career change
My son started middle school this year, and that has been particularly difficult since I had once planned to be a teacher at the same junior high. He made the basketball team, and at an away game I was surprised by how difficult it was to visit the school where I once taught. Going back to the scene of a position I once loved, where I got to help kids I really cared about, gave me delusions.
I started thinking about teaching down the road again, when my son gets older, or I get better. I had to stop myself, because I know by now it's wishful thinking. I have a health condition that isn't going away. I already know I can't teach anymore while having endometriosis. I tried, and it was nearly impossible for me.
By letting my credentials go, I finally feel free to plan my next chapter
By letting my teaching certificate go, I was able to make more room in my mind about what to do next. For instance, I know I'll be volunteering after school for my son's art club. I've also been thinking about how to help other teachers, such as creating helpful resources for students and advocating for better working conditions.
Finding ways to incorporate my teaching skills into my future work is giving me hope for what that might look like. And knowing that teaching, in the traditional sense, won't be a part of that gives me plenty of room to explore.

Airport-style passport and fingerprinting controls are to be introduced at Eurotunnel in an attempt to prevent “short-term and long-term chaos” in Folkestone and Calais.
In a breakthrough for travellers, the European Commission has agreed to a new system in which an “eagle eye” camera system, already used in Rome and Paris airports to supervise fingerprinting and facial imaging, will be used at the border between the UK and France.
Yann Leriche, the chief executive of Getlink, the Eurotunnel owner, said it had tried to replicate the “airport experience” but wanted to go much further.
Instead of getting out of the car and getting biometrics taken at a terminal building, holidaymakers and business travellers will now be greeted with special drive-through terminals in Folkestone and Calais.
Both sides are now equipped with 120 kiosks under the case of an eagle-eye camera that will be monitored by police, similar to e-gates at airports where police are not physically present at each gate.
In the coming weeks, Leriche will meet UK and French authorities presenting a 40-page proposal to allow Eurotunnel to become a “laboratory” for an “intelligent border” using emerging tech and lessons learned from the US and Singapore.
The entry and exit system (EES) requires all third-country citizens including British passport holders to submit fingerprints and facial images as they enter and exit the Schengen area, but has been delayed for years.
EES was supposed to be active across the EU by 9 September, but nine of the 27 EU member states, including France, have yet to be deploy it fully because of continued technical issues.
It has always been a logistical nightmare for Eurotunnel and a potential cause of miles-long tailbacks at the approach to the terminal.
Originally, Getlink had planned to use a tablet to hand to the passengers in their cars to allow them to self-fingerprint and capture a facial image. It also looked at a system involving passengers parking up and going into the terminal to get fingerprinting.
But both models would have required the physical presence of police officers for first-time fingerprinting.
Leriche said: “We told the authorities: it is going to be a mess. Many people are going to the wrong place and you can’t have police jumping from one place to the next to solve the issues. It would also means customers would have a bad experience, particularly at peak time.
“This is not something people in airports experience, but nobody approached this before, thinking we could have an airport experience at the border here. But we said: why not?”
He said that after “many, many discussions” with the European Commission and the French authorities, finally they were “authorised” to trial “eagle-eye cameras” at each kiosk. “The French authorities are also on board because for them it is more efficient, too, so we are all aligned on the trial,” he said.
The trial will last two years, but Eurotunnel hopes the experiment will become permanent.
Each car will be able to pull up to an individual kiosk, with two stands per vehicle to read passports and take fingerprints and facial images. “It will prevent the chaos in the long term and the short term and if the experiment works, as hopefully it will, then it will become permanent,” said Leriche.
He said the company had been inspired by visits to the US/Mexico border controls, where drivers and passengers remain in their cars.
The requirement of having a police officer present each time a first-time passenger, or “primo” as they are known, submits their fingerprints was designed as a safeguard against subterfuge. Criminals, for example, could use a fellow passenger for example with a “clean skin” fingerprint.
Leriche said he had no idea when the system will be introduced by France. “It has been delayed and delayed and delayed, but our kiosks are there, they are can function but the connection with the French system is still not working. It is a question was are asking all the time.”
This week it emerged that the EU had filed a lawsuit against IBM and two other companies involved in the implementation of EES.

What are the limitations of eGPUs vs onboard graphics cards for laptops?
An eGPU can bring desktop-class graphics to a laptop, but cables, bandwidth limits and extra costs can eat into the advantage.
Connecting a desktop graphics card to your laptop seems like a neat solution to one of the oldest problems in portable computing. Use the thin machine for work and travel, and connect to a much more powerful GPU when you get home. An external GPU (eGPU) can do just that, but all that extra graphics power still has to travel through Thunderbolt or USB4 instead of the direct internal connection used by a built-in laptop GPU. That bandwidth bottleneck can eat into the desktop card's advantage, and the cable it's connected to holds sway as well.
In this comparison, "onboard" primarily refers to a dedicated GPU built into the laptop, not the integrated graphics in the laptop's processor. Even when a laptop GPU shares its name with a desktop GPU, the hardware can be vastly different. The RTX 5090 Laptop GPU features 10,496 CUDA cores, 24GB of GDDR7 memory, and a GPU subsystem power range of 95W to 150W. Meanwhile, you'll find 21,760 CUDA cores and 32GB of GDDR7 memory on NVIDIA's desktop RTX 5090. That's a significant gap before even considering bottlenecks, like Thunderbolt.
Thunderbolt is still the bottleneck
A modern eGPU typically communicates with the laptop via Thunderbolt or USB4, rather than directly on its PCIe bus, and that's where some of the desktop card's edge is lost. A built-in laptop GPU uses an internal PCIe connection instead.
Thunderbolt 4 has 40 Gbps of overall bandwidth and requires 32 Gbps of PCIe data throughput, while Thunderbolt 5 upgrades the base speed to 80 Gbps and doubles that PCIe requirement to 64 Gbps. Internal laptop GPUs can use wider multi-lane PCIe connections, depending on the laptop's design, giving them more room to move data without the Thunderbolt bottleneck.
That bottleneck is more noticeable when it comes to a powerful desktop card. NVIDIA's desktop RTX 5090 has 1,792GB/s of memory bandwidth and a 575W total graphics power rating, compared with 896GB/s and a 95W to 150W GPU subsystem power range for the RTX 5090 Laptop GPU. Those aren't PCIe bandwidth figures, but they show how much more raw hardware the desktop card brings before the external connection starts holding it back.
Thunderbolt 5 also has a 120 Gbps Bandwidth Boost mode, but that isn't 120 Gbps of PCIe bandwidth for the GPU. Intel says PCIe data throughput remains at 64 Gbps. While USB4 can also support PCIe traffic, a USB-C-shaped port alone doesn't guarantee eGPU compatibility. The host hardware needs the right support, and the enclosure, drivers, GPU and power requirements must all cooperate (because apparently one cable was getting too easy).
Using the laptop's built-in display can add another penalty because rendered frames may have to travel back through the same limited connection. This is why some brands suggest connecting an external monitor directly to the eGPU for better performance. There's no universal performance-loss percentage, since the GPU, laptop, connection, resolution and game all affect the result.
There's a reason the built-in GPU is slower
A laptop GPU begins with less raw hardware, but it doesn't have to deal with most of this plumbing. It operates within the laptop's cooling and power constraints, doesn't have to send rendered frames back over an external cable, and remains in the laptop when you pick it up. The portability benefit is more like a suggestion with a traditional desktop-card eGPU. You now have an enclosure, a desktop GPU, and maybe an ATX power supply on the desk, while a big card can add size and noise to the mix.
Let's not forget to talk about the cost associated with eGPUs. As an example, Razer's Thunderbolt 5 Core X V2 supports full-size NVIDIA and AMD desktop cards up to four slots wide. The enclosure also has its own 120mm cooling fan, but it doesn't come with a GPU or even the necessary ATX power supply to keep it running. Those would be added expenses on top of approximately $350 for the enclosure itself.
That math gets considerably friendlier if you have a suitable GPU sitting around after a desktop upgrade. At that point, the enclosure could significantly upgrade your laptop without buying another computer. It's more difficult to justify purchasing a high-end desktop card specifically for an eGPU, especially since you're paying for all that power and then sending it through a cable that might not allow you to use it all.

The 7D fabric (which is what keeps the weight low) does need babying, but I haven't had any issues in over a year of use.

Deals on Tents
Six Moon Design's Lunar Solo is one of the best single-wall ultralight solo tents you can buy. Use the Code YULEHIKE to get the 25% off.
Nemo's Hornet tents are some of the lightest freestanding tents around. The only difference, aside from color, is that the pole segments on this model are shorter (to make it easier to store on a bike). The Copper Spur line is very nearly the lightest freestanding tent around (it's just slightly heavier than the Hornet above), and if you happen to use it with trekking poles you get what I think is the best feature, the covered awning modification for the vestibule. Vancouver duo's song goes viral after featuring in Grand Theft Auto VI
Bob Moses says Inner Light has racked up 50 million more streams since being featured in GTA trailer
Bob Moses didn’t have to steal a car, pull off a heist, or even pick up a controller to score big with Grand Theft Auto VI.
All the Canadian electronic duo needed was a killer song and an email from Rockstar Games.
They say their 2021 collaboration with British musician Elderbrook, Inner Light, has racked up more than 50 million additional streams since being featured in an extended trailer for the game in late August.
Fans have waited more than a decade for GTA VI, which finally arrives Thursday. But Inner Light has already taken on a life of its own, spreading across social media and reaching listeners far beyond the electronic music scene.
Vancouver's Tom Howie and Jimmy Vallance, who formed the Grammy-nominated duo in 2012, say their manager emailed them earlier this year with a request from Rockstar to use their song, with few details about how it would be featured.
"We were like, sweet, GTA is a big game. And then we sort of forgot about it," recalls Howie.
Months later, their phones lit up with messages from people they hadn't heard from in years.
It turned out Inner Light had landed a prime spot during the trailer’s climax, its haunting, synth-driven melodies underscoring an emotional speech about living in one’s "glory days."
"It became the part that everyone clipped and re-shared and kind of made the song go viral," says Vallance.
Spotify says the track saw a 500 per cent surge in streams since the trailer dropped, with daily additions to listeners’ playlists increasing by more than 3,000 per cent.
The unexpected success comes as musicians face mounting pressure to create viral moments in an increasingly crowded streaming landscape.
Jimmy Vallance, left, and Tom Howie of the Vancouver-based electronic music duo Bob Moses. (Hunter Monero/The Canadian Press)
Vallance says the experience reinforced something the duo has learned over years of navigating an industry reshaped by TikTok and social media: there's no reliable formula for a hit.
"You can't engineer this in a lab," he says.
"Someone somewhere liked a song that we wrote one day and put it in the trailer, and then that connected with millions of people."
The duo says they were paid a relatively modest licensing fee.
"I forget how much money it was, but it's not enough to remember," says Howie.
"The opportunity is definitely in the potential for the reach, not in the paycheque."
Toronto music supervisor Heather Gardner says that's not unusual.
Gardner, president of the Guild of Music Supervisors Canada, says a placement in a gaming behemoth like GTA can be valuable even when the licensing payment itself isn't especially lucrative.
"It's such a cultural icon," she says of the franchise.
"No one can pay their bills in exposure, but it really is in an industry that is so saturated musically right now. Everybody is looking for a way to break through and to get eyes and ears on them and a sync, beyond the payment, is absolutely that."
Music integral to GTA
Music has long been integral to the GTA experience, with the franchise’s fictional radio stations introducing generations of players to an eclectic mix of genres as they cruise city streets, mow down pedestrians and outrun police.
For GTA VI, Grammy-winning French electronic duo Justice composed the score, while Rockstar plans to release an album of original songs Thursday, featuring SZA, Tame Impala and Keith Richards.
The musical celebrations will continue into the weekend with a GTA-themed concert in Miami featuring Travis Scott and Cardi B.
Gardner says video games offer a particularly powerful form of music discovery because players aren't simply watching or listening.
"You're an active participant in the media in a way that no other form can do."
A still from the new Grand Theft Auto VI video game. (Rockstar Games/The Canadian Press)
Vallance is a longtime fan of the GTA series, recalling playing the original top-down game of the '90s on a friend's computer before becoming captivated by the leap to three-dimensional gameplay in Grand Theft Auto III.
But it was the 1980s-inspired soundtrack of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City that left the deepest musical impression, introducing him to acts such as A Flock of Seagulls and sparking an interest in the synth-pop sounds of that era.
Vallance says it's a "huge honour" his own music has now become part of the franchise's cultural orbit. The placement has also given the duo a moment of validation after years of navigating the uncertainties of a music career.
"Every once in a while something happens and you're like, 'Oh, we're a real band.'"
GTA VI is estimated to bring in $3.25 billion to $5.2 billion in first-week sales, according to market research firm Newszoo.
Howie believes the game serves as a tastemaker at a time when audiences are increasingly fragmented across countless entertainment platforms.
"There's not many things that tons of people do all together anymore. We used to all watch the same shows and listen to the same radio stations and read the same things," he says.
"GTA is one of the very few things that a lot of people still come around to; that's a unifying thing on a scale that doesn't really exist in today's age."

11 gadgets under $10 that solve everyday problems
You don't have to spend much to fix little annoyances in everyday life.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
Steve Jobs once said that customers don't know what they want until you show them. And he was right. But he was also lucky because he was showing people iPhones and not, say, rechargeable nose trimmers.
Of course, when Apple launched the iPhone in 2007, Amazon wasn't the global behemoth it's since become. Now there's virtually nothing Amazon doesn't sell, and a lot of it is dirt cheap. In the post-Bezos world, Jobsian marketing principles no longer apply. Customers still may not know what they want, but if it's cheap enough, they'll buy it anyway and then throw it out and buy something else.
Thus begins our quest to assemble a list of cheap gadgets that are worth every penny, which should come in handy around the shopping season. If you treat them right, these may last you for many holidays to come.
1. Motion sensor bathroom lights
It's the middle of the night when you wake up and need to head to the en-suite bathroom. You snap on the light and you're blinded because it's too bright. Or worse, you wake up your spouse, who can't easily get back to sleep even with their favorite sleeping app.
This scenario may sound exaggerated, but if you've ever been there, you know it isn't. Or, to spin it back to Steve Jobs, you just don't realize what you need. In this case, it's a motion sensor light for your bathroom.
Decent motion-activated lights for around $10 that don't require any drilling come in two varieties. They're either battery-powered stick-ons like the Star-Spangled LED Puck Light ($8.99 for 5), or they plug right into a socket. The latter are more like smart night lights. The BN-Link Backlit Motion Sensor ($12.34 for 2), for example, has an auto mode that only activates with motion, plus a night mode that gives a dim light until activated.
In both cases, you get to see at night without waking anybody else up. And you're good to go for years because the bulbs are LEDs and use very little energy.
2. Peel-off phone magnets for your car
Those of us driving around without built-in infotainment displays in our cars have tried every so-called solution for mounting our phones: suction cups, clips, vent mounts and more. The more expensive and heartier the holder, the faster they wilt, with one exception: peel-off phone magnets.
This WixGear offering costs $6.99 and is simple to use. First, peel off the film on the back. Stick one on the back of your phone (or preferably your phone case), stick the other on your dashboard, and bring your phone close to snap them together. It shouldn't plop to the ground ever again.
A few caveats here. One, the stickiness of the adhesive makes this a permanent fix, so don't expect to move the magnets around once they're on. Two, we recommend finding a vertical position on your dashboard that's close enough to tap, but not too close to a vent. Extreme temperature changes might lead to your phone slipping, while heat blowing on it is never good.
And three, a phone stuck to your dashboard can easily become dangerous. Don't spend too much time playing with it; you could easily get distracted. Apple has also reported that magnets can influence photo quality in certain cases, so keep an eye on that. All said, for speaker phone calls, Google Maps or playing music in your car, peel-off magnets are a tested fix.
3. Desktop/laptop vacuum cleaner
There are two types of people: those who are aware of keyboard gunk and those who have blissfully never observed it. If you don't make a habit of cleaning your keyboard, the first tool you're likely to reach for to remove gunk is a brush. You may, with much practice, reach a state of competency where you can finagle stray brush hairs into the cracks around individual keys and dislodge the detritus of your typing life that way. It works, but you can do better.
A handheld, mouse-sized vacuum cleaner may strike you as effete, and in a sense, it is. But for those who like a clean keyboard, a vacuum is quicker and much more efficient than hunting for crumbs with a brush.
Our recommendation also comes with a nozzle, brush and USB charging cable, amenities that nudge it a bit over the $10 mark. While you can find cheaper options, caveat emptor. Some of them look good but get horrible customer reviews. For best results, disconnect your keyboard from a desktop PC (or shut down your laptop) before you clean.
If you haven't kept up with other forms of computer cleaning, it's also worth learning how to clean your screen the right way.
4. A phone stand
Yes, it's just a lowly phone stand. But it could be a life-saver. If you doubt us, you've probably never had a last-minute Zoom interview where, in lieu of propping your iPhone up against a fruit bowl, you opted for a grainy, handheld shot that gave your potential employer a bold view of your inner nostrils. That isn't the only reason to invest in an inexpensive, versatile phone holder, however.
Modern versions of iOS and Android can turn your phone into a webcam, which is a great way to reuse an old smartphone. But unless you own a folding phone, you're back at square one.
A budget stand like the Nulaxy solves this problem neatly. Whatever stand you end up with, make sure it's universal so you don't have to buy one for everyone in the house. It should have a gap at the bottom to make room for the charging cable, and remain steady whether in landscape or portrait.
5. Earbud cleaners
There is perhaps nothing more disturbing than a wax-bejeweled earbud. Actually, there is: having to send your dirty, malfunctioning bud back to wherever you purchased it for a diagnosis of "ear wax accumulation." The minds behind the $6.99 Hyashee earbud cleaning pen are on our wavelength here.
Hyashee's earbud cleaners are geared toward AirPods, though the flocking sponge and brush combo will get the job done for any other brand too. As an alternative, there are other universal options like the Midukit cleaner kit. At $9.99, this comes with everything from the Hyashee Cleaner Kit, plus blobs of purple putty and some brushes. Dirt sticks to the putty so you can get it out that way.
Investing a few dollars in an earbud cleaner could improve the longevity of your buds, which makes a difference if you own a quality pair of AirPods. It could also save you from the disgrace of having to send your grimy headphones to a horrified technician at Best Buy. This applies even more if you've got kids with earbuds of their own.
6. Bluetooth camera remote shutter
There always ends up being someone who appears less often in family photos because they're the one behind the camera. To restore balance to your family, consider a remote Bluetooth camera shutter. The ATUMTEK Wireless Camera Remote Shutter is a popular choice; it's $8.99 and comes as a two-pack. It should pair with your phone up to distances of ~30 feet, and is compatible with both Android and iOS.
The Zttopo Wireless Bluetooth Camera Shutter Remote is about the same price. Reviews for both hover around 4.5 stars on Amazon. Just be warned that you'll need a tripod (or at least a stand, as above) before you assemble your first full family portrait.
7. USB thumb drive (as a portable antivirus)
You might not even need to buy a new flash drive to make this work; rifle around in your desk drawer and if you get lucky, you'll unearth a dust-covered treasure from 2011. If you can't find one — or if this is a stocking stuffer for techy friends or relatives — you can always order something like a basic Sandisk 32GB USB 2.0 drive around $9.99.
Why would you want to turn a USB stick into a portable antivirus? Because it might be all you need to clean up an infected Windows machine without having to call the Geek Squad. There are plenty of other neat ways to use an old USB thumb drive aside from storage, but this is our favorite.
When an attack strikes, it can take over your OS, locking you out of your antivirus. When you boot up an antivirus from a separate disk (your USB drive), you can bypass the infected system and clean it from the outside. ESET SysRescue Live is one example that's bootable from a flash drive.
8. Magnetic kitchen timer
For many of us, the main duty of our Google Nest Hub or similar device is to serve as a bark-activated kitchen timer. "Hey Google, set a timer for 20 minutes!... Stop!"
Considering the expense, why not just buy a digital kitchen timer? They're a lot cheaper and you won't have to bark at Google ever again. This minimal DALSHABET timer kind of looks like a Google Nest Thermostat, which is to say, it looks pretty good. It's also magnetic, so it sticks to your refrigerator or any other magnetic surface in the kitchen. And it's cheap at $9.99, though it could drop a little depending on sales.
The only part you might have to get used to is setting it manually. But that's just a twist of the dial. Is this extra manual labor worth it? If you want to save money and avoid adding yet another sporadically obedient screen of dubious utility to your home, this little $10 dial should last you a while.
9. Webcam covers
As with many aspects of digital hygiene, there are competing views on webcam covers, as well as various methods for physically blocking access to your computer's camera.
Former FBI director James Comey admitted to taping over his laptop's camera. Meta CEO and former human Mark Zuckerberg was photographed doing the same in 2016. If you're worried that your camera might accidentally pop on when you don't intend it to, a set of $8 BLOCKED vinyl webcam stickers might be useful. Keep in mind that an attack's goal is more likely to install malware or trick you into handing over credentials than to spy on you.
If you're on a Mac, the camera will never turn on without its accompanying green indicator light. You may also damage your screen if you slap on a traditional slide cover, since razor-thin laptop design doesn't allow room for them. That said, for work laptops or desktops you've had for a while, a vinyl sticker is low-cost protection against suddenly appearing at a team meeting in your pajamas.
10. USB adapter kit
If we ever calculated how much time we've lost, as a species, to USB-related inconveniences, we would drag USB's creator before the ICC. His name is Ajay Bhatt, by the way, and he's been hiding in broad daylight reaping the fruits of his evil genius since 1996.
Yes, it's just a cable. But oh, what havoc USB can wreak. The problems are endless, but the source of our grief is usually the same: we have the wrong connector for a device. Our machine could also feature the wrong port for the cable we're trying to use. Or, if we're on an Apple laptop, we probably don't have enough ports. In all three cases, we're stuck.
The usual solution is to buy an adapter, but that can still run into issues. Maybe the adapter only works for one situation, like USB-A to USB-C. Or we shell out way more for a multi-purpose hub that has ports handling a bunch of different connections, including HDMI. Fortunately, there's a middle route that costs a lot less: a USB adapter kit.
This 12-piece IANFAN USB kit, at $8.59, offers a bunch of adapters that should cover any USB compatibility issues you face. If you want a handier solution geared to USB-C compatibility, try the Povdite charging cable adapter kit, which comes with a case and its own charging cable. Whichever you choose, you'll be doing your part in the fight against uncontrolled cable sprawl.
11. Wireless charging pad
Wireless charging pads present an interesting dilemma for the sustainability-conscious gadget shopper. Will replacing one accessory (a USB cable) with another (a charging pad) actually make your life easier and the planet better? Or will you just feed the yawning maw of your accessory drawer one more tasty meal?
A charging pad still needs to be powered by a cord, so it's not truly wireless. But once you plug it in, you won't have to worry about USB compatibility anymore, as long as your devices all support wireless charging. If you can find a quality charging pad that powers multiple devices, that's even better. But that can get tricky, especially when your budget is 10 dollars.
Cheaper charging pads also might not charge as quickly, as outputs vary. And one station might not be enough for a whole household. That said, if you want to test the waters, this NANAMI Fast Wireless Charger Pad costs $9.99. It works with Android phones, iPhones and even earbuds, with a maximum charging power of 15W.

Federal officials on Thursday announced new funding to explore the medical potential of ibogaine, a controversial psychedelic drug championed by veterans, conservative lawmakers and podcasters aligned with President Donald Trump.
Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said his department is awarding up to $4.9 million to prepare for the first U.S. studies of ibogaine for post-traumatic stress disorder, a hard-to-treat condition linked to higher suicide and substance abuse rates among veterans.
The money will not go directly to patient research, Kennedy said, but to lay the groundwork needed to manufacture, dose and design studies of the drug.
Ibogaine is made from a shrub native to West Africa. It can cause intense hallucinations, nausea, vomiting, tremors and sometimes deadly irregular heart rhythms. Ibogaine is currently illegal, in the same ultra-restrictive class as LSD, ecstasy and most other psychedelic drugs.
Veterans organisations and psychedelic advocates contend that ibogaine has great promise for intractable conditions such as PTSD, severe depression and opioid addiction. U.S. research on the drug has essentially been frozen for decades due to ibogaine's restricted status.
Kennedy said the government will receive data and treatment guidance from Beond Inc., a Texas-based company that has treated more than 3,000 patients with ibogaine in Mexico, where the drug is not illegal.
“That is going to allow us to dramatically accelerate the clinical trial process,” Kennedy said. “We’re going to have, I think, a record drug approval process.”
Additional funding awards may explore ibogaine's use for addiction, he said.
Veterans Affairs Secretary Doug Collins, who joined Kennedy for the announcement, said the collaborative effort would focus first on safety and “best-in-class research.”
“For veterans living with PTSD, we owe them both urgency and the best science we can produce,” Collins said.
Kennedy and Collins have previously voiced support for the potential of psychedelics, citing the experiences of veterans who have traveled abroad for therapy with ibogaine and other mind-altering substances.
Thursday's announcement was previewed in April, when Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to speed up review and research of psychedelics that could help with mental health conditions.
Three applications for psychedelics are pending review at the Food and Drug Administration. They include the first potential medicines made from psilocybin, the active ingredient in magic mushrooms, and MDMA, also called ecstasy. Decisions on those drugs could come within weeks or months.
Because of its safety risks, ibogaine research has moved more slowly.
The little data currently available mostly comes from patients who have traveled to Mexico or other countries where ibogaine is not heavily regulated. Ibogaine clinics typically charge $10,000 to $20,000 for one course of treatment, which often involves monitoring of a patient's heart readings while emergency medical workers are on standby.
Trump's order on psychedelics came after podcaster Joe Rogan said he texted Trump about ibogaine, which he repeatedly has discussed on his show. According to Rogan, the president quickly responded: “Sounds great. Do you want FDA approval? Let’s do it.”

Six goals to go - will McGinn catch Dalglish & Law?
- Published
As Scotland legend Kenny Dalglish watched one of his records equalled in Scotland's 2-1 win over North Macedonia, another of his feats loomed into view.
The night was supposed to be about Andy Robertson joining Dalglish as Scotland's most-capped man, the Tottenham left-back making his 102nd appearance for his country.
But instead, for the first time, the 75-year-old might be nervous that his crown as one of Scotland men's all-time top goalscorers is wobbling.
That is because, in Scotland's rather humdrum Nations League victory, John McGinn - in his 94th Scotland appearance - took two big strides towards the record.
The Aston Villa midfielder now has 24 goals for his country - six shy of Dalglish's long-standing record of 30, shared with Denis Law.
"It's something that's been in the back of my head," McGinn admitted in the post-match debrief. "If I start climbing that table, it means we've been successful as a team."
Now 32 years old, time is running out for him. But as he pulls level with Hughie Gallacher, one of the Wembley Wizards of folklore, his ambition is clear.
McGinn 'definitely capable' of reaching record
There was a time when talk of this record being toppled seemed laughable. Scotland has produced strikers in recent decades, but none close to Dalglish or Law.
The fact a midfielder might take the title makes McGinn's feat all the more astonishing.
His prowess in front of goal is no secret to the Tartan Army. There was the spell at the end of 2019 where he scored six in three games, his overhead kick against Austria, his late winner against Croatia in 2024.
But of late, his lack of goals and even his performances have had some fans questioning where he fits into the Scotland team.
"It has been a bit of a dry patch for me over the last year on the goal front," McGinn admitted, and he's not wrong.
He failed to find the back of the net for Scotland in 2025, the first time he'd done that since 2020.
But, just as his form at Villa has sky-rocketed, he came up big for his new international head coach Sebastien Pocognoli.
"Isn't it great to have a John McGinn in your team?" former Scotland winger Pat Nevin said on Sportsound. "He's somebody you'd want to have in your team to be taking a penalty for you.
"I'd be surprised if John McGinn doesn't get the goal record now. It might take him another year or two, but he is definitely capable of getting that record."
'The best person I've met in football'
Becoming Scotland's main penalty taker will help, a fact McGinn alluded to coyly post-match.
In his career, he had only taken one spot-kick before this season - scoring for Scotland in the 3-3 draw against Norway back in 2023.
In this campaign he has scored three and missed one, smacking the bar against Fulham on Halloween.
In classic McGinn fashion, he bounced back to slot home against Manchester United the following week, before being caught on ref-cam admitting to the official that he was nervous to take it after his hitting the woodwork.
That jovial, lovable personality has not just won him fans off the pitch. It is clear that his team-mates at both Villa and the national team adore him.
"He's not going to stop until he [gets the record]," said striker Che Adams, who helped set up McGinn's first against North Macedonia.
"Everyone's pleased for him, he's the best person I've met in football. For him to get the recognition he deserves is amazing."
McGinn's iconic status in Scottish football is secure and will not be tarnished if he fails to climb the mountain.
Whether it is being speared by Steven Thompson in training, calling Scotland performances 'jobby', or admitting he would "probably be at Yeovil" were it not for his backside, the midfielder has already won the heart of a nation.

Methane blast kills 2 at Colombian mine, search continues for 2 missing
A methane explosion at a mine in central Colombia killed two workers and left two others missing, mining officials said
BOGOTA, Colombia -- Rescuers continued searching Saturday for two miners missing after an explosion killed two workers at a mine in rural central Colombia, officials said.
The National Mining Agency said on social media that rescuers were working at the mine, but a collapse caused by Friday’s methane gas explosion was hampering their efforts. Four miners were at the site when the blast occurred.
The mine is in Chita, a municipality in the department of Boyaca, about 149 miles (240 kilometers) north of Bogota. Boyaca Gov. Carlos Amaya said he was monitoring efforts to determine what caused the explosion.
Security camera footage broadcast by Colombian media showed a massive plume of black smoke and flames rising from the blast.
Mining officials did not identify the operator or specify what mineral was being mined. They said the mine was properly registered with the agency.
Mining accidents are common in central Colombia, where dozens of small-scale operators run coal and emerald mines.
The agency has previously warned that gases and dust can accumulate in coal deposits, creating hazardous conditions.

Remarkable progress, but cancer won't be cured in the near future: Siddhartha Mukherjee at HTLS
Oncologist and author Siddhartha Mukherjee said several cancers of the intestinal tract and the stomach "are really quite endemic" in India
Cancer will not be cured in the near future, oncologist and author Siddhartha Mukherjee said on Saturday, even as he pointed to remarkable progress against some forms of the disease.
In a conversation with HT’s Editor-in-Chief R Sukumar during the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit, Mukherjee spoke about how far humans understand life, how the rush to AI risks starving basic science in the US and India, where the line on gene editing should be drawn, and why science depends on agreeing on what words mean.
On whether advances in immunotherapy, genetic sequencing and AI meant cancer could now be cured for sure, Mukherjee said: "We can say for sure we can't cure it. That I'm pretty sure about, at least in the near future."
His explanation was the breadth of the challenge. "I think every cancer is different," he said. "We have made remarkable progress against, for instance, breast cancer, leukemias, lymphomas." A child with leukaemia whom he had treated with T-cell therapy in Bengaluru, and whose story he told in his talk, "is likely cured", he said.
Several cancers of the intestinal tract and the stomach "are really quite endemic" in India, he said, "and I'm not sure that we can clearly foresee a cure for those in the near future". He called a recent drug against KRAS, a protein involved in pancreatic cancer, "a huge breakthrough". "But the idea that we will ever cure every cancer in sort of one fell swoop, I think, is just a mistaken idea."
He was asked whether the focus on AI in medicine had come at the cost of fields such as cellular engineering and synthetic biology. Mukherjee said there were two answers —an intellectual one and a commercial one—and the commercial answer was "unfortunately, more relevant".
Intellectually, the fields reinforce each other, he said: AI is helping cell therapy, immunotherapy and synthetic biology, and the collaboration between Immuneel, the Bengaluru cell-therapy company, and Manas AI, the drug-discovery company he co-founded, involves finding new binders between cells.
Commercially, "when the pendulum swings and AI becomes fashionable", scientists who work on cell therapy are "led away" because "their grants can't get funded", he said. Scientific regulators need to "counterbalance the commercial forces" so that fields such as synthetic biology, fundamental chemistry, physics and biology "still remain funded".
"And one of the great crises in this current administration is that the commercial has overrun the intellectual," he said of the US.
"It's actually true for India too," he added. "When it becomes fashionable to talk about AI and becomes no longer fashionable to talk about fundamental chemistry or fundamental biology, we lose that balance and that has very long consequences."
Mukherjee went back to Vannevar Bush, who shaped American science policy after the Second World War, and the idea that curiosity-driven basic science is the "bedrock" on which disciplines such as medicine are built. "If you disrupt the bedrock, obviously the consequences will be felt for everything," he said.
Under "this current administration in the United States at least", he said, the commercial "has been allowed to overtake the bedrock". The consequences, he said, "are not felt in the five of years, but are felt in the tens of years".
Asked where the line lies now that science can edit genes, Mukherjee pointed to a distinction he draws in his book, The Gene, between "human emancipation", by which he means the elimination of disease, and going beyond it.
Most diseases do not depend on single genes, he said, and changing several genes, especially in a human embryo, is not easy. Some diseases are exceptions. "An important disease in India, for instance, sickle cell anemia, is actually very amenable to CRISPR-mediated technologies," he said.
"There is a real possibility that you can enhance abilities," he said, such as parts of human anatomy, noting that a single gene controls much of human musculature. But there are "strong reasons to believe that CRISPR should not be used for that", he said, because it would divide people into "those who are able to access these technologies, and those who are unable to access these technologies".
Asked whether a career spent telling the stories of genes, cells and cancer had changed his understanding of life, he said: "How could it not?" He added: "In science, history does not so much repeat itself as it reverberates." Science advances, he said, when people agree on the meaning of their terms: "The colloquial is the enemy of constructive debate."
Mukherjee, who won the 2011 Pulitzer Prize for General Nonfiction for The Emperor of All Maladies, co-founded Manas AI in 2025 with LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman.

IndiGo flight returns to Pune after landing gear fails to retract mid-air
All passengers and crew members on board flight 6E 0623 were de-boarded safely after the emergency landing, and no injuries were reported. IndiGo was arranging another aircraft to take the affected passengers to Guwahati.
A Pune-Guwahati IndiGo flight with 192 people on board returned to Pune airport on Sunday after its landing gear failed to retract shortly after take-off, officials told news agency PTI.
All passengers and crew members on board flight 6E 0623 were de-boarded safely after the emergency landing, and no injuries were reported. IndiGo was arranging another aircraft to take the affected passengers to Guwahati.
The aircraft, registered as VT-IZE, reported a technical problem soon after taking off. The pilot informed Air Traffic Control (ATC) that the landing gear had not retracted and remained extended, Pune airport authorities said in a statement.
The airport authorities coordinated with the ATC, the airline and other agencies. The Indian Air Force (IAF), which manages the airport, declared a full emergency and activated the prescribed emergency response procedures.
Fire services, ambulances and other emergency response teams were placed on high alert to ensure the safety of passengers and crew, the statement said.
As a precaution, the aircraft made a low pass over the runway so that its landing gear could be visually assessed. It then landed safely at Pune airport at 9.04 am, officials told PTI.
After landing, the aircraft was escorted to Bay No. 7 by three fire engines and two ambulances. The ATC withdrew the full emergency at 9.10 am after confirming that the aircraft was in a safe and normal condition.
An aerobridge was subsequently connected to the aircraft, and everyone on board was safely deboarded. IndiGo was arranging an alternative aircraft from Bengaluru to Pune for the passengers' onward journey to Guwahati.

Former England head coach Eddie Jones praised his old side as "very good" as they tore his Japan apart 78-15 on Saturday, but warned the All Blacks will be "violent" against them next week.
Following South Africa's defeat to France in Paris on Friday, victory for New Zealand against Wales in Cardiff would have seen them claim World Rugby's No 1 ranking, and take charge of the Nations Championship southern hemisphere table.
Instead, the All Blacks suffered their first defeat to Wales since 1953 in a shock 35-28 loss up against an immense Welsh defensive effort, and next play England at Twickenham next Saturday.
"England were impressive against Australia, they beat them quite easily," Jones said at his post-match press conference.
"They played powerfully, they played direct, and when they had the ability to shift the ball, they moved the ball accurately and quickly to space. We saw that again today.
"Well, they're [New Zealand] violent after a defeat.
"They're usually violent, very physical. They'll be massively disappointed with that performance [in Cardiff] today.
"New Zealand next week, they'll be back to the old New Zealand. They'll be hard and tough, and physical around the breakdown.
"I thought England were very good. It kills me that Will Joseph - I gave him his first cap - scores five tries against me! That's not being very loyal, is it?
"He's a great kid, mate. He always was going to be a good player.
"I have to take full responsibility for our [Japan] performance. Clearly we weren't good enough today.
"We thought we had a good preparation for the game, but obviously it wasn't good. Without making any excuses, getting the red card early in the game put us on the back foot, and we really never recovered from that, which good teams are able to do.
"We're not good enough in being able to recover from disappointments. That's clearly the case."
Borthwick: Joseph took his opportunities well - 'There's thinking to do around selection'
Joseph - who England head coach Steve Borthwick failed to select since taking the role in 2023 until Saturday - was the main topic during the home side's press conference.
While Borthwick wasn't effusive in his praise of the wing, he did admit he now had some extra thinking to do around selection ahead of facing the All Blacks.
"He took those opportunities really, really well," Borthwick said.
"Talking about the point of difference he has in his carry - we wanted the ball in his hands as much as possible, and that's exactly what happened.
"It was off the back of all the players, everybody doing their jobs in the middle of the pitch, and that creates those opportunities on the edges.
"His pace, acceleration and footwork is a real asset. And part of today, as I said before the game, was that we want to build a squad, not a team.
"Now there's some people who really put their hand up with quality performances, and it means that competition for players, the depth in the squad, and the level of experience has taken another step forward.
"There's some thinking to do around selection ahead of next week, and I'm still waiting for the medical report, which hopefully all the players come through pretty well tonight.
"I'll get that full medical report, and then I'll make the call for selection when Test week starts tomorrow night."
What's next?
For England, they next face New Zealand in their third Nations Championship Test of the autumn at Allianz Stadium Twickenham on Saturday, November 21 (2.10pm kick-off).
Japan travel to face Scotland at Murrayfield in Edinburgh for their next Test, also on Saturday November 21 (2.10pm kick-off).
