Trigger Warning: Images of physical injury
A group of around 40 men allegedly ambushed a house church in Rayan village in West Bengal’s Purba Bardhaman district on November 1, and physically assaulted the pastor and several Christian worshippers during a Sunday prayer service. The attackers accused the congregation of converting Hindus by luring them with incentives, and also accused them of running a ‘honey trap’.
Survivors told Alt News that they were forced to chant ‘Jai Sri Ram’, and were told, “This is a Hindu area; worshipping Jesus will not be tolerated”.
Several worshippers sustained severe injuries after the attack. Survivors said they were left traumatised without administrative protection or assurance. A written complaint was submitted at Burdwan police station. However, the survivors alleged that they were forced into withdrawing the complaint as attackers entered the police station and threatened to kill the complainant.
Alt News spoke to pastor Chottu Ruidas, who was leading the Sunday prayer service, and other survivors of the attack. Recounting the incident, Ruidas said the congregation had assembled at Sushanta Majila’s house around 10 am, and the service was nearing its conclusion, with the worshippers participating in communion, when a group of approximately 40 men descended on the house church, raising ‘Jai Sri Ram’ slogans.
According to Ruidas, Bisweshwar Choudhury, an influential and wealthy resident of the village who is known for helping people in need, was part of the group. He approached Ruidas during the prayer service and allegedly slapped him.
“Thereafter, the goons accompanying Choudhury started beating us mercilessly,” Ruidas told Alt News. “They slapped us, kicked us and beat us with the bamboo sticks they were carrying. They even took off their belts and whipped us.”
Ruidas said a 17-year-old boy sustained a severe head injury, leaving him bleeding profusely. “The goons told him, ‘We have treated you. Now go to a doctor and get it fixed,” he recounted.
The attackers allegedly dragged worshippers out of the house and beaten up. Those who attempted to seek refuge in neighbouring homes were pursued and assaulted, Ruidas said.
“After the goons beat us, the other attendees locked me inside a kitchen to keep me safe. But they broke open the door and dragged me out. My elder sister hugged me and fell to the ground while trying to protect me. But they continued kicking us. My sister eventually fell unconscious, and I had to take her to a nearby dispensary,” he said.
Ruidas told Alt News that he had attempted to contact police while hiding inside the kitchen but could not get through. He subsequently informed Pastor Jose Bernard, who then contacted the cops.
Bernard told Alt News that he called the Burdwan police station two to three times, but the police allegedly did not take the matter seriously. He eventually dialled the emergency helpline, 112, following which police personnel reached the village.
Bernard said his wife and minor daughter were also among the worshippers present at the congregation. By the time police reached the location, several miscreants had fled the scene. He claimed that when police entered the premises, the remaining miscreants accused the worshippers of having picked a fight with them.
Then, according to the pastor, instead of taking action against the attackers, police detained 20 women, three minors, and eight men from the Christian congregation.
Bernard categorically denied allegations of forceful conversion or conversion through inducement.
Worshippers Detained, Threatened by Accused inside Police Station
The detainees were first taken to Bardhaman Medical College and Hospital, where a doctor examined them inside the vehicle. Then, they were taken to the police station and kept in two separate rooms.
Pastor Jose Bernard subsequently submitted a written complaint at the police station. However, shortly afterwards, a group of alleged attackers entered the police station, grabbed him by the collar and threatened him with dire consequences unless he withdrew the complaint. He alleged that this happened in the presence of police personnel.
“They entered the police station, grabbed me by the collar, physically intimidated me and threatened to kill me if I did not withdraw my complaint. And all of this happened in front of the police,” Bernard told Alt News.
According to Bernard, police merely told the men, “There are CCTV cameras here; leave the premises’. That’s all.”
Bernard said that the threats and intimidation eventually compelled him to withdraw the complaint. He told Alt News that he had pleaded with the miscreants and police to at least ensure that Christians in Rayan village would not be subjected to further harassment. “This is our government. A Hindu government. A Hindu country. Worshipping Jesus is not allowed. They have to bathe in the Ganga, and we will perform ‘ghar wapsi’,” Bernard recalled them saying.
Bernard further alleged that the inspector in-charge, Debabrata Mukherjee, questioned the congregation about why they had assembled to pray in the first place. When the attendees and Bernard attempted to reason, Mukherjee allegedly asked why they were taking such risks when people were being assaulted for doing so in several places.
Eventually, the women were released from the police station around 11 pm, while the men were released around 1 am.
Speaking to Alt News, Burdwan IC Debabrata Mukherjee denied the allegation that the attackers entered the police station and threatened Pastor Jose Bernard to withdraw the complaint.
He said, “They submitted a complaint and, after some time, retracted it. No one threatened them inside the police station,” adding that “Counter-complaints have been filed against them by locals.”
Asked why the injured were detained at police station for long hours, Mukherjee claimed their families hadn’t turned up to take them home.
The officer refused to answer further questions over phone.
Elderly Woman Assaulted at Home
Another attendee, Sagari Konai, managed to escape the initial attack and returned to her home. However, a group of men allegedly went to her residence and assaulted her. She sustained a fracture in her finger due to the assault, the pastors added.
Ruidas alleged that the men forced Konai to perform sit-ups while holding her ears and apologise for practising Christianity. She was also allegedly coerced into participating in Hindu rituals at a nearby temple.
Konai is an elderly widow who lives with her daughter.
The attack has left the survivors deeply shaken. Ruidas said that he was still in pain from the injuries he sustained and that he was afraid to return to his home in Rayan village. He is currently staying with Bernerd.
Bernerd, meanwhile, said the incident had a profound impact on his young daughter, who witnessed the violence firsthand.
“She has never been exposed to such brutal hatred unfolding before her eyes. I wonder whether these people are animals,” he said.

She lost her sight - now she is fighting to make history for Africa
- Published
Rukayat Taiwo Suleimon only took up sambo this year, but the Nigerian has already secured her place in the history of the martial art.
The sport shares strong roots with judo and wrestling, combining techniques such as hip and leg throws to take opponents to the mat, where they can be pinned.
Originally developed by the Soviet Union's Red Army in the 1920s, it was officially recognised as a combat sport by USSR officials in 1938.
Competing at the 2026 World Sambo Cup in Armenia, Suleimon defeated Uzbekistan's Charos Ortikova in the final of the women's 54kg category to claim victory on her international debut.
It was the first time that women with visual impairments had been included at the competition.
"Being the first female blind sambist in the world to win the gold medal makes me great," the 32-year-old told BBC Sport Africa.
"This is my first time in sambo and God crowned my efforts."
Suleimon's achievement was part of a breakthrough moment for African women in the sport. She and compatriot Elizabeth Aseso, who competed in the 59kg category, were among the pioneering sambists representing the continent in Yerevan.
For Suleimon, her gold medal is a reward for the hard work over many years which has seen her move from athletics to judo and now to the top of the international sambo podium.
"I really benefit a lot from sports and, despite my blindness, I achieve a lot," she said.
"If I [were] not blind, I don't think I would be at this level. I believe I will achieve even more."
From darkness to double glory
Suleimon's journey to becoming a champion has been marked by hardship and a determination to rebuild her life.
After failed surgeries she lost her sight in 2009 because of glaucoma, an eye condition that damages the optic nerve and can lead to permanent loss of vision.
The change in her circumstances affected her relationships, leaving her feeling isolated at a time when she needed support the most.
"People looked down on me. I would just stay indoors and cry," she explained.
"So many friends left me. They stopped communicating with me."
Her life began to take a different direction after she attended a vocational training centre for blind people in Lagos.
Through a friend, she was introduced to a para-athletics coach who helped her discover her potential in sport.
Since 2011, Suleimon has won more than 20 national medals across sprint events (alongside guide runner Stephen Oyelakin), discus and shot put.
She then began practicing judo and sambo.
"Since I [started] sports I have seen that where there is life, there is hope," she said.
"What sighted people can do, a blind person can do even better.
"I'm proud of myself because it's not easy to be a champion in athletics and in sambo. I don't want to lose the glory."
Her achievements have also become a source of pride for her family. Her twin sister Ganiyat Kehinde Suleimon says her sibling's disability has never defined her worth.
"She is someone we are all proud of. She is now a champion," Ganiyat told BBC Sport Africa.
"Her disability did not make her a liability to us."
For Nigerian sambo coach Olugbenga Adekahunsi, Suleimon's performance in Yerevan offered a glimpse of what she can accomplish with the right support and continued development.
"I see a lot of quality in her because she is very strong and the confidence is there," he told BBC Sport Africa.
"I believe she will become a great sambist."
'No support' for para-athletes
Suleimon says the recognition she has earned internationally has not been matched by adequate "support" at home.
However, her victory is the latest milestone in Nigeria's growing presence in the discipline.
Two years ago Samuel Oladele Kekere became the first blind African to compete at the World Sambo Championships in Kazakhstan, and Sodiq Ajibade followed that with a bronze medal at last year's edition in Kyrgyzstan.
"Despite making Nigeria and the whole of Africa proud, there is nothing to show for it," Suleimon said.
Her concerns reflect wider complaints from Nigerian para-athletes about limited funding, inadequate specialist facilities and insufficient institutional backing, despite their achievements.
Sherif Hammed, vice-president of the Sambo Association of Nigeria, says a lack of resources can prevent talented athletes from reaching their full potential.
"When athletes do not have facilities to train, they cannot compete at the world level," he said.
"It is quite disheartening and heartbreaking.
"People with disabilities, particularly visually impaired athletes, sometimes feel that because of their challenges, they have no purpose in life."
For Suleimon, a Lagos State judo champion, the journey to training is also an issue. Travelling across the city and covering transport costs make maintaining a demanding schedule difficult.
"I leave home at 5.30am to make it to training on time," she explained.
"It takes a lot of money and sacrifice."
Suleimon was unable to follow up her World Cup success at the World Sambo Championships in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, where blind women were again scheduled to compete for the first time.
Beaten in Friday's opening round by Moldova's Ina Cernei, she still hopes her exploits on the global stage can inspire others.
"I want to encourage my fellow blind Africans to believe they can do it," said Suleimon. "And I want to make my country proud again."

Some people aren't ready to let former CEO Jensen Huang go.
A petition to reinstate Huang as Nvidia's CEO has some 97,000 signatures as of Saturday morning, including prominent tech leaders such as billionaire Elon Musk and Replit CEO Amjad Masad. Both executives promoted the petition on X.
A website for the campaign, dubbed "Stand with Jensen," said the list includes more than 51,000 shareholders, more than 5,100 current Nvidia employees, and nearly 900 former employees.
It also, to be fair, included "Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor" and "Xi Jingping," a possibly misspelled reference to the Chinese leader. In an X post on Saturday, the organizers said they were "actively working" to remove fake signatures.
Earlier this week, Nvidia's board of directors said it opened an investigation into whether Huang was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort" after he admitted to having an affair in a letter to staffers. Days later, Huang resigned after reports he had another affair with an Nvidia executive, and the board appointed Colette Kress, executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO until they find a permanent successor.
An October report by The New York Times said Huang had developed a "close relationship" with Alice Huang, a tech executive at Megaspeed in Singapore. The Times reported that US intelligence officials said she may be a spy for the Chinese government. China has since denied that claim. On Thursday, Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Department of Justice had not concluded whether Alice Huang was a spy.
The "Stand with Jensen" organizers said in an open letter to Nvidia's board posted to its website that they believe the board removed Huang without an investigation and "meaningful due process."
"We have not been shown evidence substantiating the espionage allegation. After thirty-three years pouring his heart and soul into NVIDIA, Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice," they said.
The organizers say they want Huang to remain CEO while the investigation continues.
"Disclose its scope and timeline, give him a meaningful opportunity to respond, and provide a clear, evidence-based explanation demonstrating that any removal is in NVIDIA's best interests. The campaign does not treat espionage allegations as proven facts or presume the inquiry's findings," the organizers said.
The "Stand with Jensen" petition also garnered signatures from big names such as Boom Supersonic CEO Blake Scholl and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan. A signatory who describes himself as an engineer at Nvidia called Huang an "essential part" of the company in a comment on the website.
"His private affairs are none of my business, and if his actions violated our code of conduct, it has to be dealt with. Please bring him back and give him fair treatment, taking his track record and importance for NVIDIA and the wider community into account," the employee said.
In a statement, Nvidia's board of directors said it will consider internal and external candidates in its quest to replace Huang, who cofounded the company and served as CEO for over three decades. The board has not publicly identified a new CEO, but the names of potential candidates have begun to surface among analysts and investors.

North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
- Published
State-sponsored hackers from North Korea have taken more than $400 million in cryptocurrency by using fake video calls to steal people's identities, US authorities say.
More than 900 victims have fallen prey to the scheme, which the FBI refers to as FaceStealer, in the last 18 months, according to the bureau.
"The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program, stealing billions of dollars in recent years," says FBI cyber director Brett Leatherman.
This comes a week after the world's largest crypto exchange Binance revealed that hackers had used fake job interviews to steal a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) from the company.
US law enforcement agencies attributed the Binance hack, thought to be the largest crypto hack to date, to North Korea-linked actors. Pyongyang has denied this claim.
Authorities say FaceStealer, the latest scheme, "aggressively targets" those who work in the cryptocurrency and web3 sectors, particularly those who are involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software.
According to the FBI and US Justice Department, FaceStealer hackers use fake or hijacked social media accounts to invite potential victims into video calls hosted over "imposter versions" of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet.
Next, the hackers play pre-recorded videos of previous victims the target is acquainted with to simulate a legitimate call – except that the audio would appear to malfunction.
A message then pops up on the target's screen, asking them to "fix" the audio by clicking on a link. This "fix" would eventually download malware onto the target's device, which allows hackers to access their contact lists and apps, widening their pool of potential victims.
Hackers would secretly record these calls and use the recordings as material to scam their new victims, according to the US authorities.
The FBI has described FaceStealer as "a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user".
"It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships," Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the bureau's Los Angeles field office, said in a statement on Thursday.
"If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough."

U.S. envoys meet with Putin in the Kremlin after Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
MOSCOW — U.S. President Donald Trump's envoys met Thursday with President Vladimir Putin as Washington sought new momentum in peace efforts after two days of U.S.-mediated negotiations between Russian and Ukrainian delegations.
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who is also Trump's son-in-law, brokered the talks in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates. Those were the first direct discussions between representatives of Moscow and Kyiv in nine months as the push for peace stalled.
The two days of talks that ended Wednesday produced no major breakthrough, aside from an agreement to swap a large number of prisoners, with the exact figure still to be announced.
Kushner and Witkoff went straight to the Kremlin to brief Putin in a meeting that lasted about two hours and are scheduled to fly to Dublin, Ireland, for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as the conflict stretches toward the five-year mark.
U.S. envoys want Europe at the negotiating table, too
Kushner said that one of the goals of the meeting with Putin was to get the Russian leader's blessing for European representatives to be part of the talks, which are looking at the continent's broader security arrangements.
The U.S. and Zelenskyy want Europe to appoint a single person to negotiate with Moscow.
But Moscow doesn't want European countries involved in the direct negotiations, complaining they are financing and supplying Ukraine's military effort. The Europeans are concerned about Russia's conduct and broader intentions on the continent.
Many in Europe see the inclusion of Moscow in discussions about postwar European security as an unwelcome concession to Putin, who has described NATO's eastward expansion as a main security threat to Russia. Putin has demanded the trans-Atlantic alliance's troops be pulled back from Russia's borders.
Some analysts say negotiators may be looking to grant Russia concessions on NATO's strategy in return for peace in Ukraine — a possibility that alarms European leaders.
The Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi "agreed on many of the principles, but are still apart on some of the way to accomplish" peace, Kushner said in Moscow.
Putin reaffirmed to the U.S. envoys that any European troops sent to Ukraine after a ceasefire would be "absolutely unacceptable" and Russia would regard the deployment as a security threat and legitimate targets. "In other words, the war would resume immediately," he said.
He also said Russia regards its border with Ukraine to be sealed by a prospective peace deal as now extending to cover the four Ukrainian regions that Moscow annexed in 2022 but never fully controlled.
Zelenskyy sees a political "window of opportunity"
Zelenskyy is in Dublin for a meeting of more than 40 European countries that also includes NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte.
Rutte said the U.S., Europe and Ukraine are "very much aligned" on what security guarantees should look like, following a meeting in Paris in January. "But now of course we need the peace deal, or at least a ceasefire," Rutte said.
Zelenskyy said political changes, including Democrats taking over the U.S. Congress in January following midterm elections and balloting in France next year, could bring "a window of opportunity" for a peace deal.
"The political landscape in Europe could change in 2027. … We also see changes already taking place in the United States," Zelenskyy said in Dublin late Wednesday.
He called the proposed prisoner exchange a positive step but also insisted Ukraine won't surrender Russian-occupied territory in return for peace.
Russia and Ukraine have occasionally swapped prisoners, but both sides remain far apart in their terms for accepting a settlement.
Fighting continues as another bitter winter approaches
Amid the negotiations, fighting continues along the 1,200-kilometer (about 750-mile) front line.
Russia's bigger army has been held back by dogged Ukrainian resistance while Moscow's drone and missile strikes on Ukraine's energy facilities disrupted heat, electricity and water supplies to Ukrainian cities, sapping public morale in what Kyiv calls a "weaponization of winter."
Russia's Defense Ministry said its air defenses downed 71 Ukrainian drones overnight. Its forces struck a drone-manufacturing plant in Kyiv and three other facilities producing missile fuel and drone components in the area around the Ukrainian capital, the ministry said.
Russia launched missiles and 123 drones, 73 of them jet-powered drones, at Ukraine overnight, the Ukrainian air force said. Hits were recorded at 17 locations, it said.
U.S. Starlink problems return, Zelenskyy says
Ukraine is experiencing another slowdown in the U.S. Starshield system — SpaceX's military-grade version of the Starlink satellite internet service — that the country needs to defend itself against Russian attacks, Zelenskyy said Thursday on social media.
Military units have recorded "significant disruptions," including speed restrictions limiting Ukrainian drones to 161 kph (100 mph), Zelenskyy said, adding that a military investigation established that the restrictions weren't random errors.
Ukraine uses Starlink and Starshield for intercepting Russian drones and launching its own strikes.
Last month, limits on Ukrainian drone speeds severely disrupted operations and alarmed Kyiv officials who fear U.S. support could drop off.
Elon Musk acknowledged that his company SpaceX had throttled the Starlink internet service in Ukraine for about a week, saying the system couldn't be used for offensive strikes against Russia.
Zelenskyy said in Dublin that the speed limits cover operations in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine and that Kyiv is trying to find out from U.S. officials what is going on. "If someone in America is making decisions that basically treat Ukrainian territory as if it is not Ukrainian, then this tells us where things are going," he said.
Russian colonel reportedly killed by a car bomb
A Russian serviceman was killed in St. Petersburg early Thursday when his vehicle exploded, according to Russia's Investigative Committee, the country's main criminal investigation agency. It didn't identify the victim or say who was behind the bombing.
The Fontanka news outlet said the victim was a colonel and that a bomb in his car exploded as he drove off.
Several senior Russian military officers have been killed by bombings and other attacks that Moscow blames on Ukraine. Kyiv has claimed responsibility for some attacks on Russian soil.

In November, a claim (archived) circulated online that the U.S. Air Force had held Maj. Jason Watson, an active-duty airman who publicly called for the impeachment of President Donald Trump, in solitary confinement for more than 80 days while he awaited court-martial.
CNN reported that the Air Force ordered Watson into "pre-trial confinement" on Aug. 18. Two days later, on Aug. 20, Watson's lawyer Christopher Mutimer told CNN that Watson was "basically in solitary confinement." He repeated this claim in early October, telling CNN (at 1:46, archived) that Watson was "still in solitary confinement."
One X user who claimed Watson remained in solitary confinement in early November — 84 days after the Air Force first ordered him into pretrial confinement — wrote:
Maj. Jason Watson has been in 24-hour solitary confinement for 80+ days & has reportedly lost 20 pounds, all before any trial. UN experts consider solitary beyond 15 days to be torture. He offered to resign, give up all his benefits, & the Air Force said no. Because he protested.
The claim also circulated on Facebook and Threads (archived, archived). Snopes readers contacted us about the claim.
Speaking to Snopes on Nov. 10, Mutimer confirmed Watson had been detained at Maryland's Calvert County Detention Center since Aug. 18 and described conditions that he said met generally understood definitions for solitary confinement.
Mutimer said Watson "is in a room by himself 22 to 23 hours a day. No one stays in there with him, he is not allowed to have any interaction. When he's let out it's to shower, make a phone call, get some time in the yard by himself." He described Watson's cell as a "pen" where "the light is on all the time."
Mutimer added, "Because he's an officer, he is in the military, that contract says he is not allowed to be with anybody who is not in the military."
A spokesperson for the Department of the Air Force said in a statement on Nov. 13:
The Department of the Air Force can confirm that Maj Watson is not being held in solitary confinement. Maj Watson is held in administrative protective segregation—not punitive solitary confinement—at the Calvert County Detention Center (CCDC) pursuant to an official Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between CCDC and the 11th Wing Security Forces Squadron (11 SFS) at Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling (JBAB).
Maj Watson is physically separated from CCDC's civilian general inmate population to comply with military policy and statutory segregation mandates. While separated from civilian detainees, Maj Watson does have regular access to standard institutional amenities and programs, including the facility library, religious services/chapel, and physical fitness time. He also retains normal access to defense counsel, military leadership visits, medical care, and personal visitation.
Because of the opposing descriptions of Watson's confinement from his lawyer and the Air Force, we leave this claim unrated. we leave this claim unrated.
By November, the docket of the Air Force's military justice branch showed Watson was due for general court-martial in February. Mutimer said he would argue a petition for Watson's pretrial release on Nov. 17.
Mutimer also confirmed the claim some social media users made that Watson had attempted to resign after his July 1 arrest but said officials had denied his resignation and instead pressed ahead with the court-martial, a move that Mutimer described as "absolutely unheard of."
Tracking Watson's case
Capitol Police arrested Watson on July 1 on after he publicly called for Trump's impeachment while wearing his Air Force uniform. A live stream (at 50:56) of the arrest showed Watson standing on the Capitol steps in uniform while holding a sign that read "Impeach Convict Remove."
Watson said at a news conference earlier that day that he was calling for Trump to be impeached because he thought the president and Vice President JD Vance had governed in an unconstitutional way throughout their administration.
Watson highlighted the war in Iran, Elon Musk's sweeping cuts to federal government and the Department of Homeland Security's immigration crackdown and killings of protesters as "high crimes and misdemeanors" (at 28:28) for which "the president and vice president must be impeached, convicted, and removed."
The Air Force major repeated his call for Trump and Vance's removal while speaking to CNN's Erin Burnett (at 1:52) on Aug. 17. Burnett said (at 2:41) during the interview that the military had placed a "gag order" on Watson after his July 1 protest and that he was "under investigation."
According to a later CNN report, the Air Force took Watson into pretrial confinement days after he spoke to the network.
CNN reported that the Air Force charged Watson with 10 violations of three articles of the Uniform Code of Military Justice, the military's legal framework, on Aug. 20. Mutimer reportedly spoke to Watson on that date and reported that he was "basically in solitary confinement."
On Sept. 29, The New York Times reported that an Air Force investigating officer had recommended Watson's case for general court-martial, the military's highest level of trial court.
According to the Judge Advocate General's Corps Department of the Air Force, which investigated and charged Watson, the major faced charges of four violations of articles 88, 92 and 133 of the UCMJ.
Article 88 (Page 34) of the UCMJ states that any commissioned officer who uses "contemptuous words" against certain public officials, which includes the president and vice president, should face a court-martial. Article 92 (Page 35) states that a person subject to the code that fails to obey an order or regulation can be subject to court-martial. Article 133 (Page 48) states that "Any commissioned officer, cadet, or midshipman who is convicted of conduct unbecoming an officer and a gentleman shall be punished as a court-martial may direct."
The code does not explicitly define what "conduct unbecoming an officer" means.
An Air Force spokesperson reportedly told Military.com in October that the Air Force had acted in accordance with the Rule for Court-Martial 305 when it took Watson into pretrial confinement in August. That rule says someone can be placed in pretrial confinement if there is probable cause they committed "an offense triable by court-martial."
That rule also says that someone taken into pretrial confinement can ask a military judge to review the "propriety" of the confinement, meaning whether it is appropriate. Mutimer said such a review for Watson would happen on Nov. 17.
According to the UCMJ's Article 13 (Page 5), it is prohibited to punish a service member awaiting trial. Any confinement before trial must not "be any more rigorous than the circumstances require to insure his presence, but he may be subjected to minor punishment during that period for infractions of discipline."
At the time of this writing, Watson had not been convicted or sentenced. Punishments for service members convicted by court-martial range from reprimands and salary reductions to dismissal or discharge.
For further reading, Snopes has previously investigated whether an active-duty soldier took part in an anti-immigration-enforcement protest.

In the Israeli legislative elections held in late October 2026, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party and its allies secured 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, falling short of the 61-seat majority required to govern. The Yashar party, led by Gadi Eisenkot, alongside other opposition factions, won 48 seats. Notably, Arab-led parties made historic gains, winning 19 seats and becoming potential “kingmakers”. Following the vote, President Isaac Herzog formally accepted the results. He opened a two-day consultation window with party leaders to determine who is best positioned to assemble a stable coalition.
In this context, a video is being shared on social media (here, here, and here) with the claim that it shows the Palestinian flag being hoisted in the Israeli Parliament. Let’s verify the claim made in the post in this article.
Claim: The video shows the Palestinian flag being hoisted in the Israeli Parliament building.
Fact: The video does not show the Palestinian flag being hoisted in the Israeli Parliament. It shows a pro-Palestine activist replacing the German national flag with a Palestinian flag on a flagpole outside the Reichstag building, which houses the German Parliament (Bundestag), in Berlin on 08 November 2026. Hence, the claim made in the post is FALSE.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to multiple media reports (here, here, and here) featuring visuals similar to those seen in the viral video. According to these reports, the incident took place outside the Reichstag building, which houses the German Parliament (Bundestag), in Berlin on Sunday, 08 November 2026.
The reports (here, here) state that a 22-year-old pro-Palestine activist climbed a 30-metre-high flagpole in front of the Reichstag building at around 11:30 am, removed the German national flag, and replaced it with a Palestinian flag.
The group ‘Peacefully Against Genocide‘ claimed responsibility for the incident, stating that the action was a protest against the German government’s pro-Israel policy and its silence on alleged human rights violations in Gaza.
According to a press release issued by Berlin Police on 08 November 2026, two people who allegedly assisted the 22-year-old activist were detained and later released after their identities were established. The Palestinian flag was subsequently removed with the assistance of the Berlin Fire Brigade. Police also launched an investigation into suspected offences, including insulting state symbols, damaging government property, trespassing, and violating Berlin’s assembly law.
To sum up, the viral video shows the Palestinian flag hoisted outside the German Parliament, not the Israeli Parliament.

NEW DELHI: An 18-year-old saleswoman was found murdered inside the trial room of a clothing showroom in west Delhi's Moti Nagar on Saturday evening, with police identifying a 29-year-old man as the prime suspect.
The victim, identified as Shabnam, was allegedly attacked with a knife before the accused fled. Police have formed teams to trace and apprehend the suspect, identified as Suraj, a resident of Sudamapuri in Moti Nagar.
Her body was discovered inside the trial room of Vastr Mahal, located at 6/18, Moti Nagar. She had a sharp injury on her neck, and a blood-stained knife was recovered near her body, police said.
A woman claiming to have witnessed the events leading to the discovery of the body said Shabnam had previously worked for her before joining a shop directly opposite her workplace.
"The girl used to work for me... She had started working at a place right across from mine. At around 6.45 PM, I noticed her—I could see her shop from my own—sitting there and using her phone," the woman said.
She said she received a call from Shabnam's employer around 7.30 pm, informing her that the young woman was missing after a man allegedly assaulted her.
"Around 7.30pm, I received a call from her employer, who said, 'I don't see Shabnam in the shop. 
A man came by and beat her up quite severely. Could you please go and check what happened? She is nowhere to be found, and she left the shop wide open.' I went over, but we couldn't find anything..." she said.
The witness said two neighbours later arrived at the showroom, closed the shop and locked it around 8 pm. However, after checking the CCTV footage, they returned around 8.30 pm, suspecting that Shabnam might still be inside.
"Then, around 8.30pm, the men came back to me and said, 'Shabnam must still be inside—we checked the footage, and she never left. We only saw a man leave, but she didn't come out. Could you come inside with us to take a look?'" she said.
The group entered the showroom while recording a video. The woman said they initially found nothing, before noticing Shabnam's scarf near the trial room.
"We went inside while recording a video, but we couldn't see anything at first. Then, my eyes fell toward the very back—the trial room—where I spotted her scarf (chunni) lying on the floor, and blood was seeping out from inside..."
The woman said they immediately alerted the police and contacted Shabnam's parents.
"We immediately called the police and contacted Shabnam’s parents... Her throat had been slit, and she was lying on the floor, with blood everywhere," she said.
A PCR call reporting a woman lying unconscious inside the showroom was received at Moti Nagar police station on November 14. A police team reached the spot and found Shabnam dead.
Crime team personnel and forensic science laboratory experts subsequently inspected the scene and collected evidence. Her body was shifted to the mortuary of Deen Dayal Upadhyay Hospital for a post-mortem examination.
During the preliminary investigation, police found that two of the suspect's brothers are married to two sisters of the deceased.
Based on a complaint lodged by Shabnam's brother, police registered a murder case under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Police teams later visited Suraj's residence but found it locked. Investigators are probing the motive behind the murder and efforts are underway to trace the suspect.

Congo's Ebola cases have crossed 11,000 cases in another development that shows the severity of the outbreak.
Also Read: Congo’s Ebola outbreak tops 10,000 cases as authorities race to slow spread in African countries
The latest Health Ministry data on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) showed 11,042 people have been infected by the deadly virus that has now killed 5,387, nearly half of those infected, in the country's deadliest outbreak.
Since the outbreak was declared mid-May, Congolese authorities have struggled to contain it due to a series of factors including conflicts and a health system crisis.
The Bundibugyo virus responsible for this outbreak has no known vaccine or treatment and has spread to the eight of the country's 26 Provinces.
Dozens of Ebola outbreaks have been reported since the disease was first discovered in 1976. The largest and deadliest occurred in West Africa from 2014 to 2016, with 28,000 infections and more than 11,000 deaths.
The current outbreak already ranks second, and has had at least three times the number of cases and deaths in the time since it was declared compared with the West Africa outbreak. Health officials declared the outbreak in May, but medical evidence suggests infections were occurring months earlier.

- Says technology must serve human welfare; calls upon graduates to turn demographic dividend into responsibility.
- 130 of 163 gold medals go to women at Cluster University convocation
Jammu- Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha on Saturday said artificial intelligence would provide speed and access to data, but humans must provide direction, stressing that technological advancement must be guided by civilisational values, accountability and human welfare.
Addressing the first convocation of Cluster University of Jammu, Sinha said the relationship between artificial intelligence and humans would be one of partnership rather than competition, adding that while AI would transform the way people work, determining the purpose of that work would remain a human responsibility.
“AI will have speed and data, but humans will provide direction, compassion and the courage to ask new questions. AI should be guided by civilisational norms, values and accountability, and its development should rest on human welfare, not just profit and productivity,” he said.
Emphasising the importance of humanities in an increasingly technology-driven world, the Lieutenant Governor said, “Technology tells us what we can do, while the humanities teach us what we should do.”
He said the country needed engineers as well as historians, and scientists as well as musicians, to strengthen society’s intellectual wealth and capabilities.
Calling upon young people to turn opportunities into meaningful contributions, Sinha said he preferred to describe India’s demographic dividend as a “demographic responsibility”.
He said society would benefit when young people connected farmers to markets, transformed women’s self-help groups into employment-generating enterprises and developed affordable medical tools for remote areas.
“Don’t just seek opportunities, create them,” he told the graduates, while advising them to present well-researched solutions to companies’ challenges during internships rather than simply seeking opportunities.
The Lieutenant Governor also suggested that students strive to become valuable members of the organisations they work with and choose internships that offer opportunities to learn new skills.
Highlighting India’s growth in science and technology, Sinha said the country was witnessing a historic period of transformation, with significant progress in digital public infrastructure, space research and innovation, quantum technology, artificial intelligence, semiconductors, green energy and biotechnology.
Referring to India’s startup ecosystem, he said the country had nearly 223,000 startups and 135 unicorns, with several entrepreneurs emerging from smaller towns, reflecting the democratisation of opportunities.
He urged the graduating students to contribute towards the national resolve of building a developed India by 2047, saying the goal would be closely linked to their own professional achievements.
“Building a developed India by 2047 is our national resolve. By then, many of you will be at the highest peaks of your careers. Therefore, a developed India is not a slogan for another generation; it will be the essence of your life’s achievements,” he said.
The Lieutenant Governor also highlighted Jammu and Kashmir’s intellectual heritage, referring to Maharishi Kalhana, Maharishi Abhinavagupta, and the saint-poets Lal Ded and Sheikh-ul-Alam, saying they promoted harmony among faiths and the pursuit of truth.
He said the graduates were carrying forward a tradition of knowledge spanning more than a thousand years.
On the occasion, Sinha particularly lauded women students for winning 130 of the 163 gold medals awarded at the university’s maiden convocation.
He said the achievement reflected the growing accomplishments of women in higher education and demonstrated that when given opportunities, daughters did not merely attain positions but redefined the meaning of achievement.
Describing their gold medals as “badges of confidence” for future generations, he said women across higher education institutions in Jammu and Kashmir were writing new chapters of success.
The Lieutenant Governor also outlined five resolutions for the graduating students: never stop learning, create opportunities rather than merely seek them, uphold honesty and ethics, support those who follow and express love for the nation through action.
He reminded the graduates that their degrees marked the beginning of a new journey and encouraged them to embrace continuous learning, courage and compassion.
“Knowledge without character is meaningless,” he said, urging students to have the courage to speak the truth, do what is right and treat every human being with dignity and respect.
Governor of Tamil Nadu Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar also attended the convocation.
Vice-Chancellor of Cluster University of Jammu, Prof K S Chandrasekar, presented the university report.
Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, Minister for School Education, Higher Education and Jal Shakti Shamim Firdous, Registrar Ankur Mahajan, heads of departments, faculty members, students and their parents attended the ceremony.
Member of Parliament Jugal Kishore Sharma, MLA from Jammu West Arvind Gupta, heads of various educational institutions, prominent citizens and senior civil and police administration officials were also present.

Littler beats Greaves to start Grand Slam defence
- Published
Luke Littler started his Grand Slam of Darts title defence with a comfortable win over Beau Greaves on the opening night in Wolverhampton.
The 19-year-old cruised past Greaves with a 5-2 victory, finishing with an average just under 110 and seven 180s.
The world number one raced to a 3-0 lead before calmly withstanding Greaves' threat of a fightback in the best-of-nine match.
Littler is unbeaten in 15 Grand Slam matches, and is aiming to become the third player after Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen to win three successive titles.
"I am happy with the win," Littler told Sky Sports.
"I said in my pre-match interview I needed to get off to a strong start because Beau started to find it at the end there.
"Beau was fantastic but I am happy with myself and still 100% here in Wolverhampton.
"I think it is what I need. Obviously the past three or four majors haven't gone well, but I have been practising and I am glad I have shown it."
Last month, Littler was knocked out in the quarter-finals of the European Championship after he was also beaten in the semis at the World Youth Championships.
The expanded tournament sees 48 group stage matches being played across the opening three days.
Luke Humphries, who won the World Grand Prix title in October, beat Paolo Nebrida to begin his campaign while fellow Englishman and two-time major winner Ross Smith suffered a shock 5-3 defeat by youngster Rusty-Jake Rodriguez.
English debutant Henry Coates, 20, held his own against Van Gerwen but the three-time champion won the deciding leg to clinch a 5-4 win.
There were also wins for Gerwyn Price, Nathan Aspinall, Stephen Bunting and Dutchman Gian van Veen.

Tesla is doubling, or perhaps tripling down on its bold claims of an autonomous future with the offer to “select customers” to purchase a Cybercab for “personal use.” But the gilded, steering-wheel-free two-seater will “only be available in supported service areas” — meaning you’ll only be able to buy one if you live in one of the cities where Tesla currently operates its Robotaxi service.
Tesla is inviting some people to buy a Cybercab ‘for personal use’ — but read the fine print
Look past the $29,990 sticker price and the math — and regulatory risk — gets messy fast.
The price of a Cybercab is listed at $29,990, plus a mandatory $299-a-month “Autonomy Subscription.” Tesla’s Robotaxi account on X announced the new offer, including screenshots of the order page and the invite email. But don’t expect a fleet of personally owned Cybercabs to suddenly materialize on public roads: “Initial availability is limited,” the invitation email warns.
Tesla began offering rides in the Cybercab as part of its Model Y-powered Robotaxi service in Austin in September. The company now has 278 Cybercabs in operation, representing approximately 40 percent of its fleet, according to the crowd-sourced Robotaxi Tracker.
The inclusion of a mandatory $299/month subscription is sure to rankle some fans who may have dreamed of cruising around in a $30,000 driverless Tesla, as originally promised by Tesla CEO Elon Musk when he first introduced the Cybercab in 2024. Musk made no mention of the Autonomy Subscription at that event, though it shouldn’t come as too much of a surprise given the $99/month fee Tesla currently charges for its Full Self-Driving (FSD) feature.
Still, that money adds up over time. Over a standard 5-year ownership period, the mandatory $299/month fee adds $17,940 to the sticker price (even with the first month included), bringing the real baseline cost to roughly $47,600 before taxes, charging, and insurance — more than a brand-new Model 3 or Model Y that you can actually drive anywhere in the country.
Unlike a standard Tesla where canceling FSD just reverts the car to manual driving, canceling the $299/month Autonomy Subscription renders the Cybercab completely unusable on public roads because there is no manual fallback. In effect, the car becomes a brick. Additionally, Tesla says that buyers will have to put down a $1,000 non-refundable deposit just to get in line for a December delivery window that isn’t guaranteed.
One of the biggest selling points of Musk’s 2024 “We, Robot” pitch was that regular people could buy a Cybercab and add it to Tesla’s Robotaxi network to earn passive income while they sleep or work. But the order terms explicitly prohibit owners from using the vehicle for commercial purposes — meaning no Uber, no DoorDash, and no putting it on Tesla’s own Robotaxi network to offset the $299/month fee. Tesla AI chief Ashok Elluswamy has floated Q2 2027 as a possible target for letting customer cars join the network, so early buyers are paying full freight with zero way to monetize the car.
Moreover, Tesla only has to give you 30 days’ warning before raising the price. If they update the rules and you keep using the service, you automatically agree to the new terms. Also, if you cancel — or if Tesla suspends your access — you won’t get a partial refund for the rest of the month you already paid for.
Of course, that’s just the fine print. On X, Tesla CEO Elon Musk was promising a much wider rollout, subject — of course — to “regulatory approval.” Musk frequently frames regulatory approval as the primary external bottleneck holding back his robotaxi timelines as a way to shift focus away from Tesla’s technological shortcomings.
(For what it’s worth, he also called his own company’s $299/month Autonomy Subscription “too high,” arguing that it should actually be $115/month or closer to Tesla’s $99/month Full Self-Driving subscription.)
But Musk seemed more focused on taunting YouTuber Marques Brownlee, who promised to shave his head if Tesla delivered a Cybercab for under $30,000 before 2027, than answering any of the litany of safety and liability questions raised by this offer. (For his part, Brownlee says he thinks his hair is safe.)
For starters, how does Tesla plan on selling a vehicle that doesn’t comply with current Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards that require traditional controls like steering wheels and pedals? Tesla says the Autonomy Subscription covers autonomous driving, maintenance, and towing, but explicitly excludes auto insurance. The company hasn’t explained how personal auto insurers will underwrite a car with no human driver, or how liability is split between the owner and Tesla if the vehicle causes an accident while operating autonomously. Nor has Tesla disclosed how it selects invited buyers or how many units are earmarked for private sale versus its internal fleet.
Then there is the small matter of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration already opening a formal audit into how Tesla self-certified a vehicle without a steering wheel, pedals, or side mirrors. Tesla submitted its legal justification to NHTSA in October, requested that the entire response be kept confidential, and is now taking customer deposits while NHTSA’s ruling is still pending.
Which means early buyers aren’t just paying $47,600 for a geofenced car they aren’t allowed to drive — they’re putting down non-refundable cash on a vehicle the federal government hasn’t even decided is street-legal.

Gadi Eisenkot sharply criticized Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu days after the Israeli leader attacked Arab lawmakers in a divisive speech.
Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief who is trying to form the next Israeli government, accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday of fueling a “racist” campaign against the country’s Arab citizens, in some of the strongest public criticism of his rival’s attacks on the community.
The comments were made days after Mr. Netanyahu delivered a divisive speech to the opening session of Parliament, or the Knesset, in which he referred to Arab lawmakers as “terror supporters” and “haters of Israel.” Diplomats and analysts condemned the remarks as a brazen display of hatred and incitement against Arab citizens, who make up about 20 percent of the overall population, and voted in massive numbers in inconclusive elections last month.
“Since the beginning of the election campaign, they have been subjected to a racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimization, fueled by the outgoing prime minister and those around him for political purposes,” Mr. Eisenkot said in a statement on social media.
“Arab citizens of Israel are an integral part of the Israeli story,” he said, adding that it was wrong to malign an entire community.
“The attempt to marginalize them and vilify them collectively is a profound violation of the principles of statesmanship,” Mr. Eisenkot said. “It dishonors Israel’s Declaration of Independence and the values we take pride in as a Jewish and democratic state.”
The Declaration of Independence says all citizens have equal social and political rights “irrespective of religion, race or sex.”

At least 6 killed and 11 injured when bus overturns in southwestern Colombia
Police report that at least six people are dead and 11 injured after a bus overturned on a highway in southwestern Colombia
BOGOTA, Colombia -- A bus overturned Saturday on a highway in southwestern Colombia, killing at least six people and injuring 11, the National Police said.
A police report seen by The Associated Press said the driver may have briefly fallen asleep at the wheel, causing the incident.
Videos shared on social media showed emergency personnel assisting injured passengers and people crying next to the overturned bus on the Garzon–Neiva highway. The bus, which was headed to the capital, Bogota, was later removed from the road and traffic was restored.
The police report states authorities were still trying to determine the exact circumstances under which the bus overturned in the department of Huila, but they believe the driver may have experienced an episode of “microsleep" — falling asleep for a few seconds.
Col. Edwin Correa, director of the police’s traffic and transportation division, stated in the report that drivers must ensure they have had “adequate rest before beginning a journey.”
Authorities did not immediately identify the victims.
The bus had departed from the community of San Vicente in Colombia’s southern department of Caqueta.

Nine days before Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO, I sat near the front row at a San Francisco conference and watched him discuss the future of AI.
Two things struck me that day. Both seem more significant now.
First, Huang wasn't wearing his famous black leather jacket. Instead, as you can see in the photo I took, he wore a dark fabric zip-up. At the time, I thought it was funny. His jacket had become such a recognizable part of his image that seeing him without it was a bit jarring.
Now, with revelations about his extramarital affairs and allegations involving a possible Chinese spy, I wonder whether the wardrobe change meant something. The initial allegations were already public by November 3.
Of course, that's hindsight talking. Maybe a jacket is just a jacket.
The second thing was more consequential.
Near the end of the conversation, Fireworks AI CEO Lin Qiao asked Huang about his unusual management style. He had 60 executives reporting directly to him.
Huang explained that he'd designed this structure more than 30 years ago, when personal computers and email were transforming business. Rather than a traditional hierarchy, he wanted information flowing freely among executives empowered to make decisions.
Then came the obvious question: What should a company's leadership structure look like in the AI age?
"I don't know the answer to that," Huang replied.
At the time, I thought that was a bit odd. Nvidia is leading the AI revolution and Jensen leads Nvidia. Wouldn't he be thinking of how best to run this company in the future?
Today, that exchange seems especially relevant.
With Huang gone, Nvidia faces an extraordinary succession challenge. Sixty direct reports may have worked brilliantly under its founder. But it also means there isn't an obvious deputy to take the reins.
If he'd had two or three direct reports, those people would have had more experience with more responsibility. But 60 direct reports, by definition, means that each one of those execs only had a small piece of Nvidia to oversee.
Does this mean Nvidia is doomed? I'm not sure. The way Jensen described Nvidia's structure back on Nov. 3 provides some hope.
Huang said he gave executives considerable freedom to make decisions and work together, rather than taking orders from the top. Instead of a rigid management hierarchy, Nvidia organized itself around projects, with teams forming and changing as needed.
"Irrespective of whatever internal or external threats and opportunities, the company will naturally adapt itself, it should adapt itself to new opportunities," he said. "That was the organization I created."
The talk ended on a poignant note. Again, with hindsight, I can't help thinking he knew something was coming.
"I'm super proud of you," he told Fireworks' Qiao. "Don't forget us little people someday."

As the United States and Iran remain deadlocked over negotiations to end the nearly nine-month-old war, reports suggest that the two sides are continuing discussions through Qatar in an effort to reach an agreement. Amid these developments, Israel's intelligence agency, Mossad, has reportedly informed the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) that the Islamic Republic intends to target President Donald Trump and senior members of his administration. According to a report by Israel Hayom, officials in Tel Aviv and Washington said the threats were among the main reasons behind Trump's recent shift in his approach to negotiations with Iran. Citing senior officials, the report added that Israel corroborated the intelligence at the request of the US, after American intelligence agencies asked Mossad to verify the information. Roman Gofman, the director of Mossad, is currently visiting Washington, where he has met, among others, with CIA Director John Ratcliffe. However, another official noted that Washington was already aware of Iranian threats against Trump and members of his administration following the killing of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Iran's former Supreme Leader, in airstrikes on the first day of the joint US-Israeli military operations. Israeli intelligence has pointed to specific and recent threats, including potential attacks involving drones packed with explosives, which are difficult to thwart using conventional security measures. According to reports, Trump is not the only US official facing potential threats from Iran. Other names include Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who oversees sanctions against Tehran and is considered a driving force behind the economic campaign that has inflicted significant damage on the Iranian regime. Earlier this week, Bessent told CNBC that he had been receiving death threats from Iran. Another high-profile name is Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who has taken a firm stance against reaching a peace agreement with Iran. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is also reportedly among those facing threats. All three officials have been moved to secure locations on a military base amid heightened security arrangements. Additionally, some officials reportedly on Iran's alleged hit list have reduced their appearances at outdoor events in recent weeks. As for Trump, the report noted that special protective measures have been introduced for his public appearances, including a reduction in outdoor engagements. The latest report comes amid a separate investigation by The New York Times, which reported that Tehran was considering the use of chemical weapons against its adversaries, triggering concerns among some US officials. Israeli intelligence agencies have warned their American counterparts that Iran is accelerating efforts to develop the technology required to deliver chemical weapons through missiles or covertly transport them into Israel and other countries for use in attacks. Although the intelligence has also been shared with officials in Gulf countries, several regional officials have questioned the credibility of the claims. They have raised suspicions that former Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government could be attempting to persuade the US and its partners to resume large-scale military operations against Iran. Since the beginning of the war, Israel has shared intelligence with US officials on several occasions, warning of repeated threats to Trump's life as Iran allegedly plotted to assassinate the US President. A similar warning was issued in July, when reports suggested that Tehran had devised a plan to assassinate Trump. However, US officials said at the time that Washington had not verified the intelligence. Addressing reports of a possible Iranian attack on his life, Trump told reporters at the time, "They want to take out the US leader — me." He added, "I'm on whatever list. I saw this morning I'm on every single one of their lists. And so far, I guess I've been a bit lucky, but maybe that doesn't last very long. These are evil, sick people. And we have to root out that cancer. That cancer. You know what you do? You've got to cut out cancer early. And that's the way I feel." The latest intelligence warning is now adding another layer of uncertainty to an already strained relationship between Washington and Tehran, with threats against Trump and senior administration officials emerging alongside concerns over Iran's alleged chemical weapons ambitions. While Washington has stepped up security arrangements for key officials, questions remain over the credibility and extent of the intelligence being shared by Israel and its regional partners. The developments could further complicate diplomatic efforts to end the nearly nine-month-old war. Seeing niece, 2, as obstacle to affair with her mother, Jharkhand man kills child
Police recovered a missing toddler's body from a West Singhbhum nullah and arrested her relative. The motive centred on the accused viewing the child as an obstacle to leaving with her mother.
Police recovered the body of a two-and-a-half-year-old girl from a nullah in Jharkhand's West Singhbhum district after she was pushed to her death by a relative, news agency Press Trust of India reported on Saturday.
The girl's father, a resident of Keonjhar district in neighbouring Odisha, had lodged a police complaint after she went missing on November 11. Police have arrested the accused and sent him to judicial custody.
The girl and her mother were visiting her step-uncle, Samir Pan, at his home in Narsanda village under the Muffasil police station area. During the investigation, police found that the girl had left the house with Pan on November 11 but did not return, Muffasil police station officer-in-charge Vinod Kumar told PTI.
According to police, Pan was in an extramarital relationship with the girl's mother, who is his cousin. He wanted to move elsewhere with her but considered the child an obstacle to the plan and decided to get rid of her, Kumar said.
Pan took the girl to the nullah on a pretext and pushed her to her death on November 11, the officer said.
Police detained Pan for questioning on Friday after suspecting his involvement. He initially tried to mislead investigators by claiming that he had dropped the girl home before leaving for the market, Kumar said.
Pan later broke down during questioning and confessed to the crime, according to the officer. Police recovered the child's body from the nullah near the village and sent it for a post-mortem examination.
Police subsequently arrested Pan and sent him to judicial custody, while the girl's body was recovered nearly three days after she went missing from the village.

Panamanian authorities investigate bombing attack on investigative reporter's home
Authorities in Panama are investigating a bombing attack on the home of an investigative journalist
PANAMA CITY, Panama -- A bombing attack Saturday on the home of an investigative reporter in Panama was being investigated by authorities, the newspaper “La Prensa” reported.
No one was injured in the attack targeting journalist Rolando Rodríguez, according to “La Prensa,” which publishes his work.
The Attorney General’s Office of Panama said authorities were investigating a possible case of arson but said the probe may be expanded if other crimes are uncovered.
“While this was an attack on my life and the lives of my family, I must say that it changes the rules of the game in Panama,” Rodríguez told reporters Saturday. “Because now, we are all potentially exposed to this kind of thing.”
Rodríguez is a veteran investigative journalist and columnist who has led or contributed to numerous investigations into alleged corruption and irregularities within Panama’s public sector, the judiciary and businesses.
“La Prensa” reported that the attack at Rodríguez's home came at a time when he was preparing to publish a piece implicating former officials from the administration of President José Raúl Mulino and a government contractor.
The newspaper reported that an individual arrived at Rodríguez’s home by taxi around 2:30 a.m., got out of the vehicle and threw an object toward the residence, triggering an explosion. The journalist’s wife managed to escape the house unharmed and Rodríguez was not in Panama City at the time. The newspaper said there was property damage.
Mulino took to social media to condemn the act, stating that the National Police in coordination with the Public Prosecutor’s Office were investigating the incident and gathering evidence. Mulino said Panama does not tolerate such acts under any circumstances and noted that he had reached out to Rodríguez to express his solidarity.
National and international journalists also condemned the attack. The National College of Journalists called for a rigorous and transparent investigation to identify those responsible.
“What happened in the early hours of the morning — which you have learned about throughout the day — is a matter that concerns the entire country,” said Jorge Molina, president of Corporación La Prensa. “This goes beyond the press; it is an act of terrorism. That is a harsh term, especially given Panama’s history.”

At a press conference today, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that Friday’s nationwide ground stop ordered by the FAA was related to work replacing outdated copper wire with a fiber optic line at a “remote FAA facility.” The secretary said that this was “routine maintenance,” rather than the result of a major modernization effort. He told reporters that it was “such an old wire that it was being discontinued, meaning that line was going to get shut down,” necessitating the upgrade.
Work to replace old copper wire led to the FAA’s ground stop
Issues with a new router related to a fiber optic upgrade grounded thousands of flights on Friday.
What wasn’t clear, according to Secretary Duffy, was the root cause of the problem. He said that it could have been faulty hardware, a misconfigured router, or “incompetence” on the part of contractor L3Harris. Regardless, what followed was the newly installed router “flooding” other routers in the Air Traffic Control system. Duffy said that there were “over 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds,” causing disruption to radar feeds and communication with planes.
Secretary Duffy also took the opportunity to call on additional funding from Congress for modernizing the Air Traffic Control system, and to tout the work the FAA has done so far. “We are building, we are building safely, but we are building fast,” he said, but said that Congress had only given him a “partial payment” to complete the necessary work.

Khan, who is imprisoned in Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi, had an eye check-up at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), one of the officials said on Wednesday (November 11).
“He had some blood pressure issues ... and was given required treatment last night. He has been shifted back to his prison cell,” the person said.
The cricketer-turned-politician has faced multiple corruption charges since he lost power in a no-confidence vote in 2022, and has been in prison for more than three years. All of Khan’s convictions bar one have been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending. He denies wrongdoing and says the charges are politically motivated, a claim the government denies.
Khan’s lawyers say the 74-year-old’s health has deteriorated in prison and that he has lost significant vision in his right eye.
It is the first known instance of Khan being taken to hospital for treatment and returned to jail since August, when his hospital visit was cut short.
A Pakistani court has also ordered jail authorities to allow Khan’s legal team to see him and his wife, his party said.
His party’s deputy chairman, Shah Mehmood Qureshi, was also taken to hospital in the eastern city of Lahore from a jail in the same city on Tuesday (November 10). He remains in hospital.

While this claim spread in 2026, the actual incident happened in 2020.
A claim is spreading online that a bald eagle attacked a $950 "government drone" in midair, sending it crashing into Lake Michigan.
Social media users shared the story on Facebook and Reddit, prompting Snopes readers to search the website to determine whether a bald eagle had, in fact, launched a successful attack against a foreign object in its airspace.
This story is true — although it happened years ago, not in 2026. It is also worth noting that while some posts online appear to show a bald eagle flying at a drone, there is no actual footage of the incident, according to the Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy, or EGLE — the agency whose drone lost to the eagle.
Michigan state officials confirmed the eagle's assault in an Aug. 13, 2020, news release titled, "Shoreline-mapping EGLE drone sent to watery Lake Michigan grave by U.P. bald eagle." (U.P. is a reference to Michigan's Upper Peninsula.)
Here's how that release began:
An Upper Peninsula bald eagle launched an airborne attack on a drone operated by a Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE) pilot last month, tearing off a propeller and sending the aircraft to the bottom of Lake Michigan.
The brazen eagle vs. EGLE onslaught took place near Escanaba in Michigan's Upper Peninsula on July 21 when EGLE environmental quality analyst and drone pilot Hunter King was mapping shoreline erosion for use in the agency's efforts to document and help communities cope with high water levels.
King had completed about seven minutes of the mapping flight — his fourth of the day in the area — when satellite reception got spotty. He pressed the "Go Home" recall button. The drone dutifully turned, reacquiring a strong satellite feed.
King was watching his video screen as the drone beelined for home, but suddenly it began twirling furiously. "It was like a really bad rollercoaster ride," said King. When he looked up, the drone was gone, and an eagle was flying away. A nearby couple, whose pastimes include watching the local eagles attack seagulls and other birds, later confirmed they saw the eagle strike something but were surprised to learn it was a drone. Both King and the couple said the eagle appeared uninjured as it flew from the scene of the crime.
The release also confirmed that the drone was "a $950 Phantom 4 Pro Advanced" and shared data indicating that the eagle tore off a propeller, as many of the claim posts said (emphasis ours):
Data from the flight records detailed the drone's final moments:
- The eagle strike occurred 7:39.7 into the flight roughly four-tenths of a mile from King and 162 feet above the water
- Its speed instantly dropped from 22 mph to 10. Within a half-second the flight record shows the beginning of downward spiral along with "excessive spinning" warnings
- In the next 3.5 seconds the drone sent 27 warning notifications including one indicating a propeller had been torn off
- Gaining momentum as it fell, its last communication came at 34 feet above the water, falling at 30 feet per second, or 20.4 mph.
Per the release, King and the unidentified couple searched for the drone, "but hours of scouring the shoreline were fruitless." An unmanned aircraft systems coordinator with the state agency, Arthur Ostaszewski, also attempted to find the drone using a kayak, snorkeling gear and "telemetric data from the flight that pinpointed exactly where the drone hit the lake." He, too, was unsuccessful, even after walking a grid pattern for two hours — "like I was playing Battleship and wanted to cover the entire board," he said.
A week later, however, a team of Michigan state employees — which the agency cheekily dubbed in a news release as the Willful Eagle Trauma Team Engaged in Retrieval, or WETTER — managed to uncover the drone in almost the exact same location after "the previously murky water had cleared due to shifting winds and currents." EGLE shared a few pictures of the recovery effort on X, then known as Twitter:
The agency noted that the drone was not recording at the time of the bald eagle's assault, meaning that there would not be any footage of the fight over airspace.
Michigan officials speculated that the attack could have been "a territorial squabble with the electronic foe, or just a hungry eagle."
"Or maybe it did not like its name being misspelled," EGLE said, poking fun at its agency acronym.
At the time, EGLE said it was considering steps to try to prevent a repeat attack, including adding a design to make the drones look less like seagulls. Snopes found no evidence of any bald eagle drone attacks since EGLE's incident in 2020, however, so this may have just been a one-time thing.
EGLE also said the Michigan Department of Natural Resources was unable to issue a citation or violation notice to the "rogue eagle."
"Unfortunately, there's nothing we can do," the agency's spokesman said. "Nature is a cruel and unforgiving mistress."

Paul Barril, French ‘Supergendarme’ Turned Mercenary, Has Died
After years in elite police units, he drew scrutiny from human rights groups for selling arms and providing other services to unsavory governments. He was 80.
Paul Barril’s offer to African dictators was straightforward: Your opponents will be subjected to surveillance and manipulation. Newspapers will be “infiltrated.” Plots against the state will be “neutralized.”
Plenty of heads of state took up the services he offered, including Omar Bongo in Gabon and Denis Sassou-Nguesso in Congo. Other clients went to Paris to do their shopping at his Security Action Store, which offered the latest in bulletproof vests or night-vision goggles, as Mr. Barril recounted in one of his six autobiographies, “The Elysee’s Secret Wars” (1996).
Mr. Barril was often described in the news media as a former French “supergendarme” for his longtime work in elite units. After he left the gendarmerie, or national police, in 1984, he became a security adviser and mercenary provider across the African continent and was implicated by human rights groups in the Rwandan genocide of 1994.
His death, on Oct. 20 at 80 at his home in Antibes, France, was announced by the French interior ministry. He had Parkinson’s disease.
By the time he founded his mercenary-security company, Secrets, a French acronym for Security Equipment Planning and Realization Company, in 1984, Mr. Barril was a well-chronicled public figure.
In the gendarmerie, which in France is under the military, he joined a new military police intervention unit, the GIGN, in 1974. The French news media chronicled Mr. Barril’s reputation as an ultrafit top cop, a military-grade swimmer and diver, a black belt in karate, a parachutist, a hostage liberator and a policeman working inside and outside the law. With the GIGN, he participated in the 1979 operation against Islamist militants who had seized the Grand Mosque in Mecca, taking dozens hostage.
