Rahul Gandhi joins gig workers' bike rally in Hyderabad, launches welfare scheme
Visuals showed Rahul Gandhi riding pillion on a scooty driven by a female gig worker, while Reddy was also seen riding pillion behind another worker.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi participated in a bike rally with gig workers in Hyderabad on Saturday and launched a scheme that will allow gig workers to access information about their work, completed rides and earnings through their mobile phones.
Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy and other Congress leaders also took part in the rally. Visuals showed Gandhi riding pillion on a scooty driven by a female gig worker, while Reddy was also seen riding pillion behind another worker.
Addressing the launch of the Telangana Gig Workers' Social Security and Welfare Scheme, he spoke about the growing importance of data in the 21st century and pointed out that gig workers in India had not been able to access their own data until now, news agency ANI reported.
"The 21st century is the century of data. Data is discussed across the country; data centres are being set up. Google, Facebook, WhatsApp, Uber - all of these function on the strength of data. But gig workers were not getting their own data in India until now," he said.
Gandhi added that the new law would grant them the right to access this information, with the Telangana government ensuring that details of the work they undertake, rides they complete and payments they receive would be accessible on their mobile phones.
The scheme is a part of the Telangana platform based gig workers (registration, social security and welfare) act, 2026, passed in March this year.
The act states that aggregators can terminate gig workers only for valid reasons, which must be communicated in writing with at least seven days' notice. It also requires platforms to make timely payments and ensure a safe working environment for gig workers.
Under the act, gig workers will also be entitled to ₹five lakh accident insurance, ₹10 lakh health insurance and the government will provide wi-fi enabled rest zones, he said.
‘Wi-Fi-enabled rest zones’: Gandhi
Highlighting the challenges faced by gig workers who travel long distances and make deliveries in the heat without proper resting facilities, the Congress leader said the Telangana government would set up Wi-Fi-enabled rest zones across the state.
These spaces would allow gig workers to take breaks during working hours.
"You move across the cities of Telangana under the sun; you deliver goods, but you do not have dedicated places to rest. So, the Govt of Telangana is going to set up Wi-Fi-enabled rest zones where you can park your vehicle, rest, sit, relax or sleep in Hyderabad and all cities of the state," he said, according to ANI.
Gandhi added that the launch of the scheme marked the fulfilment of the assurance given to the workers during their earlier interaction. "I had a meeting with the gig workers of Telangana. You shared your sorrow and pain with me. At that time, I said that the Congress party, our CM and all of us had promised you that we would take steps regarding your demands and we would make every effort to help you and protect you. Today, we are fulfilling that promise," he added.
Gandhi also targeted BJP, saying that the ideology of BJP-RSS is aimed at benefiting big capitalists like "Adani, Ambani" while treating workers like bonded labourers, according to news agency PTI.

There's a hidden way you can check which services are running on your Android phone
Just like a desktop PC, your Android phone has a built-in task manager. Here is how to find it, monitor your memory and safely limit background apps.
If you use a desktop PC, you may be familiar with the task manager, which lets you view all the processes running in the background of your computer and taking up resources. What you may not know is that Android phones (even budget models) have the same feature, but it's kept hidden away from users, requiring a little digging to find it. If you want to keep an eye on what's using your phone's memory, it can be worth uncovering this hidden display, but you should proceed with caution before you start closing processes willy-nilly.
To check what processes are running, you first need to activate developer mode to make your phone faster. Under the Settings menu, scroll down to the bottom, tap About Phone and look for the Build number. If it's not there, you may have to enter an additional Software information menu, depending on your phone's model and Android version. Once you find it, keep tapping the Build number option until you get a message that developer mode has turned on or a dialog box asking you to confirm. Then, back out to the main Settings menu. You'll find Developer options on this main screen, or under a System submenu. Tap the option, then open Running Services. You can also select the three dots in the top right of the screen to select Show cached processes and see what's been recently suspended but still held in memory.
Use the Running Services menu with care
This is Android's version of the task manager, showing you all the running services currently providing frameworks for the apps on your phone, along with how much memory they're using. But don't start closing processes to free up that precious memory. While the task manager on PC often shows plenty of bloat that you can safely close, that's not usually the case for Android phones. The processes you see here are more likely managing features like Bluetooth, your keyboard and location settings. Shutting these down can seriously hamper your phone.
Both the Running Services and Memory menus are more like diagnostic tools. If you're having problems with your phone, it can be helpful to check here and see if anything seems wildly out of order, like a single process hogging the majority of your phone's memory. You may want to stop the related process until you can fix the underlying issue, but be prepared to restart your phone if anything goes wrong.
There are better ways to control background processes
A better way of controlling background processes is by limiting their use. In the Developer options menu, under the Apps heading, you'll find Background process limit. This lets you limit the number of apps allowed to run in the background at one time. This default setting triggers an automatic limit based on how much RAM your phone has, which is a crucial factor in making older Android phones last longer. However, you can also change the limit to between one and four to free up memory.
Keep in mind that this will make multitasking harder and will cause a bigger performance hit at the moment you re-open apps, since your phone will have to fully restart them now.
You can also limit how individual apps behave in the background. In the Settings menu, head to Apps, select a specific app and tap Battery. The default Optimized option automatically adjusts the app's background permissions based on how you use it, but switching to Restricted limits its activity when suspended.

Former Indian cricketer Sachin Tendulkar has joined the cap table of Hyderabad-based cleantech startup Recykal. The startup did not disclose the size of the investment. In a statement, Recykal said that Tendulkar infused the capital during the extension of the startup’s recently closed $23 Mn bridge round. Back in June, the clean tech startup had raised $17.6 Mn in equity funding. The round also comprised an additional secondary component worth $5.4 Mn, which saw participation from existing backers and family offices. “What drew me to Recykal was seeing how technology was being used to solve an everyday problem. Recykal’s mission to use technology to drive behavioural change across 1 Bn people is what really connected with me, and I hope together we can encourage more people to make responsible choices every day,” said Tendulkar in a statement. Founded in 2016 by Abhay Deshpande, Abhishek Deshpande, Ekta Narain, Vikram Prabakar and Anirudha Jalan, Recykal operates a B2B marketplace for recyclable materials. It also provides software solutions to help brands track plastic and e-waste recycling to meet compliance mandates. The startup also recently launched a deposit return system (DRS), a reverse vending machine service for recovering consumer packaging. Under DRS, consumers pay a refundable deposit on containers at purchase and get it back when they return the container to a collection point. Backed by the likes of Morgan Stanley, 360 ONE, Circulate Capital and the Murugappa Group, the startup has raised more than $60 Mn in funding to date. Recykal claims to operate a network of more than 5,000 waste aggregators and recyclers and claims to cater to 650 enterprise brands, including the likes of Hindustan Unilever, Samsung and BMW. In June this year, the startup had told Inc42 that it closed FY26 with a gross revenue of ₹1,498 Cr, up 53.2% from ₹978 Cr in the year ago fiscal. However, losses jumped 7% to ₹60 Cr compared to ₹56 Cr in FY25. Interestingly, Tendulkar’s investment in Recykal comes almost two weeks after he backed gaming startup Metasports Interactive, the company behind mobile cricket strategy game Hitwicket. Besides, the retired cricket icon has also invested in a range of other startups such as used car marketplace Spinny, listed fintech startup Kissht, and former Swiggy Instamart leader Karthik Gurumurthy’s activewear brand Ten X You.

- The claim that Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth awarded a commendation medal to a different person than the soldier who reprimanded his group Nov. 11 at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is unfounded.
- The rumor stems from social media users comparing a blurry image of one side of the soldier's face with a sharper frame from a video showing the other side of the soldier's face. Aside from the apparent asymmetricality, no evidence has been offered that the images — which differ greatly in angle, lighting and distance — show different men.
- A Pentagon spokesperson told Snopes, "As shown in the photos, Secretary Hegseth welcomed the 3rd U.S. Infantry Regiment, the Old Guard, to the Pentagon where he proudly awarded Specialist Thomas Iglesias the Joint Service Commendation Medal for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on November 11, 2026."
On Nov. 11, video footage captured a U.S. Army sentinel guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in Virginia reprimanding Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and his entourage after one of them talked and laughed out loud on the steps of the monument. The next day, Hegseth was photographed ostensibly awarding that same soldier a commendation medal in a Pentagon ceremony. 
Almost immediately, posts (archived) on X and Facebook popped up comparing images of the soldier taken at the tomb with one of Hegseth awarding him the medal in an apparent attempt to sow doubts it was the same person.
People claimed the sentinel's ears looked completely different in the two images and suggested the medal recipient was a body double. Several Snopes readers asked us if it was true Hegseth gave the medal to a doppelganger instead of the actual soldier.
(X user @JamesTate121)
The argument, as summarized in one post, went as follows:
Even though it's not the same side ears, most pairs of ears are pretty symmetrical. The details of the ear of the guy he gave the comm medal to, claiming it was the soldier who reprimanded his group, is totally different shape and physical attributes.
If it were true that most pairs of human ears are symmetrical, the argument might stand, but researchers say perfectly symmetrical facial features are the exception, not the rule. When you add to that the differences contributed by angle, lighting and distance in photographs, arguing that the appearance of asymmetricality, especially in photographs, is definitive proof that a pair of ears don't belong to the same person is bound to fail.
In the above collage, a blurry image of one side of a soldier's face is contrasted with a sharper frame from a video showing the other side of a soldier's face, and it's true they don't seem very symmetrical. Does that mean both ears can't belong to the same person? Not at all. Nor has any other evidence been offered to support the claim it isn't the same man in both photographs. The claim is therefore unfounded.
Snopes contacted the Department of Defense to confirm the identity of the soldier. A spokesperson responded, "As shown in the photos, Secretary Hegseth welcomed the 3rd U.S. Infantry Regiment, the Old Guard, to the Pentagon where he proudly awarded Specialist Thomas Iglesias the Joint Service Commendation Medal for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on November 11, 2026."
As Snopes has previously reported, soldiers have guarded the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington since March 1926. The Arlington National Cemetery website states that the guards initially "discouraged visitors from climbing or stepping on the Tomb." The 3rd U.S. Infantry Regiment has guarded the monument since April 6, 1948. Barbara Starr, CNN's former Pentagon correspondent, told the network (at 11:24) on Nov. 11 that sentinels correct any visitors who do not act with "respect and silence" at the tomb.
For further reading, Snopes has investigated numerous claims about Hegseth. Snopes has also covered many "body double" claims over the years.

Jensen Huang’s exit from NVIDIA has put the spotlight on the company’s leadership and succession plans. But for India, the more consequential question is what happens to an ecosystem that has increasingly come to depend on the American chipmaker for its AI ambitions. From data centre operators ordering thousands of GPUs to startups building on its software stack, NVIDIA has established relationships across almost every layer of India's AI industry. Its influence extends beyond hardware procurement to cloud infrastructure, developer tools, technical partnerships, startup incubation and even equity investments. It is also helping Indian companies access global investors and customers. The scale of this presence is visible in the country's expanding AI infrastructure ambitions. Some of the key partnerships include Yotta Data Services committing to deploying more than 20,000 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs, while Greenko promoters-backed AM Intelligence (AMI) has announced orders for 29,000 next-generation Rubin GPUs. L&T's Vyoma, meanwhile, is developing a 10,000-GPU AI Factory using NVIDIA's B300 architecture. But these relationships are not identical. Some companies procure hardware, others access NVIDIA's technology through OEMs and systems integrators, while several startups rely primarily on its software and developer ecosystem. India's dependence on NVIDIA runs across three layers: hardware, software and commercial relationships. Competing with NVIDIA and providing alternatives to its Indian partners, therefore, requires more than matching its hardware. Rivals must also replicate its software ecosystem and industry relationships, Sanchit Vir Gogoi, analyst and founder of Greyhound Research, told Inc42. The question is whether Huang's departure changes any of these relationships, and how exposed Indian companies are to a change in NVIDIA's priorities. NVIDIA's Grip On AI Compute India's AI infrastructure buildout is increasingly being shaped around NVIDIA's GPUs. Yotta, Neysa, ESDS, AMI, E2E Networks and L&T Vyoma are among the companies making large commitments to the chipmaker's hardware, although the procurement arrangements and partnerships differ. According to Counterpoint Research, quoted by Moneycontrol, there have been commitments of over $4–5 Bn toward Nvidia's GPU-powered AI data centres. This included both AI stack and infrastructure partnerships. That dependence also has a policy dimension. The IndiaAI Mission's common compute programme relies on a network of empanelled cloud and infrastructure providers. IndiaAI Mission, which had onboarded over 45,000 GPUs by June 2026. By August, it had approved 237 projects for subsidised compute, with 93.18 Lakh GPU hours sanctioned. Any disruption in access to advanced GPUs could therefore affect not just private data centre operators but also the availability and pricing of compute for startups, researchers and government-backed AI projects. The Geopolitical GPU Game Huang's exit has exposed a geopolitical vulnerability in India's AI infrastructure ambitions: its dependence on a company whose access to global markets, political influence and supply chains is now under greater scrutiny. The concern is particularly relevant amid renewed US scrutiny of advanced chip exports. The Biden administration's 2025 AI Diffusion Rule, which had placed India in a middle tier with import caps, was subsequently suspended from enforcement by the Trump administration. However, the formal rescission process remains incomplete, according to a May 2026 Government Accountability Office assessment, as noted by Vipul Agrawal, partner at law firm Clavius Legal. More recently, reports have suggested that the US Commerce Department is considering tighter licensing requirements for advanced chip shipments to seven countries, including Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand. India has not been named in the proposed framework so far. Agrawal says India's current position is comparatively favourable, but that does not guarantee uninterrupted access. "On the US Government's published position, India currently enjoys comparatively favourable treatment for buying advanced AI chips, but that is not a guarantee of supply. Suppliers may ask more about where chips are deployed, who the customers are and where the chips may go next, which could slow procurement." He adds that Indian operators must also account for restrictions governing the subsequent transfer or export of controlled hardware. Exports of certain high-performance chips and computers containing these chipsets are only allowed on government authorisation. For Indian neoclouds and data centre operators, the challenge is therefore not limited to securing an initial GPU shipment. They must also understand the ownership structure of their customers, intended use and potential restrictions on overseas customers accessing their infrastructure. “Indian neoclouds and data centre operators must assess their obligations under the US Export Administration Regulations (EAR). This includes verifying the export classification of the GPUs, applicable licensing requirements, and the identity of the supplier, consignee, and end-user,” said Shashi Mathews, partner At CMS INDUSLAW. Indian providers must bear in mind that providing foreign nationals or restricted entities with access to controlled technology or computing power can legally function similarly to exporting the physical item, he added. Who Can Compete With NVIDIA? Meanwhile, alternatives are beginning to emerge. AMD's Instinct accelerators and Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) offer competing architectures. The IndiaAI Compute Portal's empanelment table lists 44,077 compute units from 14 bidders: 35,985 NVIDIA units, 5,548 Google Trillium TPUs, 1,096 AMD MI300X and MI325X units, 1,200 AWS Trainium and Inferentia units, and 248 Intel Gaudi units. So does India need to diversify? “Yes, by workload, and with evidence,” said Greyhound Research’s Gogoi. “Inference is where portability is closest to ready, because serving software increasingly hides the accelerator from the application.” Indian startups are also exploring different approaches. Bengaluru-based Turiyam is developing a full-stack compute platform built around inference workloads, CUDA-free middleware and RISC-V hardware. Ziroh Labs, meanwhile, is positioning its Kompact AI runtime as a CPU-first alternative, claiming NVIDIA A100-class inference performance on Intel Xeon processors. These companies are not yet substitutes for NVIDIA's large-scale GPU ecosystem. But they reflect an emerging effort to reduce dependence on a single hardware architecture. The NVIDIA Ecosystem Lock-In Hardware is only one part of NVIDIA's influence. Its software, particularly CUDA, is arguably an even more significant source of competitive advantage. CUDA, NVIDIA's parallel computing platform, allows developers to build applications that run on its GPUs. Over the years, the company has built an extensive ecosystem of libraries, development tools and frameworks around it, including cuDNN, TensorRT and its broader AI Enterprise platform. For companies developing and deploying AI models, this ecosystem reduces the time and effort required to build applications on NVIDIA hardware. Developers can use established frameworks and libraries rather than building infrastructure from scratch. This creates a significant switching cost. A company that has invested years in building its AI applications around CUDA cannot necessarily move to AMD or another accelerator simply by replacing its GPUs. It may have to rewrite parts of its software, optimise workloads and retrain engineering teams. NVIDIA has also expanded its software offerings beyond the underlying computing platform. Its NeMo framework supports the development and customisation of generative AI models, while NIM provides microservices for deploying AI models in production. The company has also developed Nemotron, a family of open models, and tools for data curation and model optimisation. And Indian companies are already using these offerings. NVIDIA has Sarvam AI, Gnani.ai, Chariot, CoRover.ai, and Tech Mahindra among adopters of its NeMo and Nemotron ecosystem. TCS, Infosys and Wipro have also been building enterprise AI solutions using NVIDIA's software stack. This software presence is significant because it creates relationships even with companies that do not directly own or operate large GPU clusters. Will Open Source Survive? Jensen Huang has also championed open source AI models and development tools, an approach that has helped NVIDIA strengthen its position among developers. Notably, NVIDIA announced that it will acquire Huggingface, one of the world’s largest repositories of open source models, for approximately $13 Bn. However, its support for open source is also commercially driven. Open models can be adapted and optimised to run on the hardware most widely available to developers. Given NVIDIA's current market position, this often means its own GPUs and CUDA cores. Rahul Sai Poruri, CEO of FOSS United Foundation, which supports and promotes open source ecosystem in India, believes NVIDIA's strategy to drive open source is unlikely to change dramatically after Huang's departure. "NVIDIA definitely benefits significantly from the existence of open models. If we have more and more closed models, such as Google's Gemini, these models could be optimised specifically for Google's hardware, including its TPUs. Open models, on the other hand, are likely to be optimised for whatever GPU is most widely available to developers. Currently, that is NVIDIA." He added that it could take several years, potentially half a decade or more, for the broader ecosystem to meaningfully reduce its dependence on NVIDIA. Huang's exit may change the company's public positioning or priorities over time. However, its software business, developer relationships and established integrations are institutional assets that are unlikely to disappear with a leadership transition. From Inception To Startup Investments NVIDIA's relationship with India extends beyond selling hardware and software; the company has also been building a pipeline of startups, investors and technology partners that can expand the adoption of its computing platforms. A key part of this strategy is NVIDIA Inception, its global startup programme. The initiative provides early-stage companies with access to technical training, developer tools, preferred pricing on select hardware and software, cloud credits and introductions to potential investors and business partners. The programme is free and does not require startups to give up equity. NVIDIA says it supports more than 4,000 Indian AI startups, making it an important channel for bringing new developers and companies into its ecosystem. More recently, NVIDIA has started making direct equity investments in Indian startups. In August 2026, it participated in a $74 Mn funding tranche for Sarvam AI, becoming the startup's first strategic investor from the global chip industry. The investment came as Sarvam expanded its efforts to build sovereign AI models and applications for Indian languages. NVIDIA also participated in Simplismart's $14 Mn Series B round in October 2026. The startup builds software to help enterprises deploy and optimise AI models and has worked with NVIDIA on technical integrations involving its Dynamo inference software. These investments are important because they go beyond the traditional customer-vendor relationship. NVIDIA is now backing companies that could become significant consumers of its hardware and software, while also helping them develop products and reach customers. For India, this could mean greater access to technical resources, compute infrastructure and global investor networks. But it also raises questions about how much of the country's emerging AI ecosystem will be built around a single technology provider. Jensen Huang's role in building NVIDIA's India presence went beyond overseeing commercial partnerships. His visits helped bring India's largest conglomerates, IT companies and emerging AI startups into NVIDIA's global ecosystem. During his September 2023 visit to India, he outlined collaborations with Reliance and the Tata Group around AI infrastructure and foundation models. A year later, NVIDIA announced a fresh wave of partnerships involving TCS, Tech Mahindra, Tata Communications and Zoho. Huang's exit does not necessarily threaten these relationships in the immediate term. For Indian companies, the immediate priority is less about who occupies NVIDIA's corner office and more about ensuring that their own businesses are not built on assumptions of uninterrupted access and are not exposed to supply chain risks.

The meme appeared to have used outdated census estimates for the population of Texas, which increased by nearly 2.5 million people between 2020 and 2025. Even still, Snopes could not replicate the meme's alleged findings.
After Democrats in Texas flipped control of the state House of Representatives and won the governorship during the 2026 midterm elections, a meme circulated suggesting there may have been election fraud in the historically Republican stronghold.
According to the meme, the number of registered voters exceeded the number of voting-age citizens in counties across the state. Several social media posts relayed the image, which showed a map of Texas' 254 counties, including on Instagram and Facebook. Some posts on X also shared the meme, including one that said "97 counties are over the adult-citizen count" (archived):
The meme claimed the counties in red had more registered voters than adult citizens, and the ones in yellow had at least 10% more registered voters than adult citizens. The image gave numbers for only six counties as evidence of its claim — Collin, Denton, Fort Bend, Montgomery, Parker and Williamson — saying that in each of them, the number of registered voters exceeded the number of adult citizens.
The meme cited as its sources the Texas secretary of state's November voter registration figures and Census 2020-24 adult citizen estimates.
We could find no evidence for the meme's claim. Using the most recent U.S. Census' adult citizen estimates (2024) in these counties and comparing them with the Texas secretary of state's numbers on voter registration per county, we could not replicate the image's alleged findings. For this reason, we rate the claim false.
The meme carried a watermark for the X account @_Patriot1776Q_. We reached out to the account asking for more information about the numbers and we will update this report should we receive a response.
It should be noted that Texas' population was the fastest-growing in the country between 2024 and 2026, and our calculations do not account for this growth due to the fact that the U.S. Census' most recent estimate for adult citizens is for 2024. (This also means that comparing the number of registered voters in 2026 to an older, smaller population estimate, as the meme claims to do, would be a flawed comparison.)
An attempt to replicate the meme's calculations
In January, the Redistricting and Voting Rights Data Office of the U.S. Census published its estimates for citizens of voting age by race and ethnicity for 2024. Snopes uploaded that data into a spreadsheet organized by state and county, with the six counties the meme mentioned highlighted them in yellow.
Next, we pulled data about registered voters and actual voters in each county in Texas. (To reflect population changes, we included July 2025 U.S. Census data and calculated the estimated number of adults, citizens and noncitizens combined, per county.)
We compiled the data for the six counties used in the meme and six more among those marked yellow — that is, counties where there were supposedly at least 10% more registered voters than adult citizens. Our calculations did not demonstrate the map's claim.
In an attempt to replicate the meme's numbers, we used the 2024 estimated number of adult citizens against the 2026 number of registered voters. For these numbers to be accurate and definitive, we would need to have 2026 actual numbers of adult citizens in these counties, as opposed to estimates.
For example, the meme said there were 34,319 more registered voters in 2026 in Montgomery County than there were registered adults based on 2020-2024 estimates. We found there were in fact 20,076 fewer adult citizens (based on the 2024 estimate) than there were registered adults in 2026.
The meme also said Parker County counted 111% registered voters relative to the number of estimated number of adult citizens. Our calculation found 108%. Once again, this number did not reflect the updated number of adult citizens in the county in 2026; Parker County is reportedly one of the fastest-growing counties in the nation.
Texas also places voters "in suspense" before removing them from the voter rolls when election officials believe a registered voter may have moved. This means that the number of registered voters reported for a county includes people who may no longer live in that county. Parker County, for example, had just under 9,000 voters in suspense in November, according to the state.
It also should be noted that voter turnout across Texas was roughly 50% in the 2026 midterms, and no county had more votes than adult citizens.
For further reading, Snopes also debunked the claim that Texas "found" 20 million votes to flip it to a Democratic majority.

Poignant gun violence message DC gym shooting survivor scrawled on a notepad from hospital bed
When Susan Hamerski’s loved ones asked her what she wanted the world to know, she picked up a notepad

A woman seriously wounded in Thursday’s deadly shooting rampage in Washington, D.C., shared a powerful message about gun violence from her hospital bed.
Susan Hamerski, of Minnesota, was shot while walking her daughter’s dog in the Logan Circle neighborhood, suffering “serious and severe” injuries, family friend Tina Wilcox, who is speaking on behalf of the family, told The Washington Post.
Hamerski is in stable condition but cannot speak. When loved ones asked her what she wanted the world to know, she picked up a notepad and wrote: “Gun control is public health,” Wilcox said.
The Minnesota woman has made it past the life-threatening stage of her injuries, Wilcox said Friday evening, though her recovery timeline remains uncertain. Her family has asked for privacy as she continues to recover.
Hamerski was among five people struck by gunfire after doctor Matt Wade Lambert, 55, killed a manager inside the Vida Fitness gym before opening fire on people from the balcony of his $1.1 million penthouse, according to police.
The incident began when Lambert fatally shot James Stuart, 46, the manager of his condominium building. Lambert became increasingly angry over a long-running dispute about black mold in his seventh-floor penthouse, police said.
After shooting Stuart with a handgun inside the gym, Lambert left the building and returned to his penthouse. From his penthouse balcony, he then used a rifle to fire at people outside, striking five victims, none of whom lived in the building. Two of those wounded were construction workers on a nearby crew.
Lambert then “barricaded” himself inside his penthouse, where he allegedly started a fire and fired shots through the door. He then took his own life using one of the three guns he had, police said.
It has since emerged that Lambert was embroiled in a bitter legal dispute with Stuart and the Metropole Condominium Association over the condition of his penthouse, which he called “psychological warfare.” He reportedly spent $300,000 fighting the dispute, draining his retirement savings, according to his attorney.
In December 2025, Lambert spoke with Washington Sun reporter Michael Brice-Saddler about the conflict, using what the journalist described as “intense, combative language.”
Lambert reportedly told a neighbor who also had complaints about the building: “If you want to see the building manager, he comes in the gym about 8 o’clock.”
During the interviews, Lambert also made a passing reference to Luigi Mangione, who pleaded guilty in connection with the 2024 killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.
“What are they called? Delay, deny, defend … the Luigi three?” Lambert reportedly said, referencing the phrase inscribed on Mangione’s bullet casings.

In China’s Spy Operations, Romance Can Be a Long Game
Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman U.S. officials say is a Chinese spy has drawn attention to the role of intimate relationships in espionage.
At the height of the Cold War, a top official in China’s intelligence agency said that his country would never use seduction to entrap a person.
Such tactics might be for the C.I.A. or the K.G.B., the official named Kong Yuan, of the Central Investigation Department, told a group of agents in training in April 1960, but China was guided by principles. He looked at the few female comrades in the audience. “Rest assured, we will not be asking you to go run beauty traps.”
Despite that pledge, captured in a 2010 memoir by a former Chinese diplomat, China’s intelligence services have for decades used romantic entanglements to compromise or extract information from prominent people.
American officials say that China’s Ministry of State Security, which runs intelligence operations today, recruited a Chinese businesswoman to collect intelligence on Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia and one of the most powerful figures in the artificial intelligence boom.
It was not clear what role the woman, Alice Huang, or Huang Le, might have had with the Chinese spy agency. Ms. Huang was a top executive of a Singapore company that operates data centers in Southeast Asia using Nvidia chips and that rents their computing power to Chinese firms.
Mr. Huang has acknowledged that he had an affair with Ms. Huang. President Trump has said that Mr. Huang told him that he was not aware that the woman was a spy. China has rejected the espionage allegations against Ms. Huang, calling them smears against the country. U.S. officials have not provided evidence for their claims. Ms. Huang has not responded to requests for comment.

One cable mistake could be killing your desktop PC's gaming performance
Your monitor might be connected to the motherboard instead of your graphics card, and the fix takes only a cable swap.
You may have a great graphics card in your gaming desktop and still be disappointed with its performance because of where the monitor is plugged in. Many PCs have HDMI, DisplayPort and USB-C monitor connections in two places: on the motherboard and on the dedicated graphics card. The same cable can fit either set of ports, which isn't particularly helpful.
If your desktop has a dedicated graphics card, the monitor should normally connect to that card's outputs. You may end up with less capable integrated graphics or a blank screen if you use a motherboard port. Instead of assuming that the problem is your hardware, start by inspecting the back of the case. The motherboard's video outputs typically use the graphics integrated into the CPU (if it has any), instead of the dedicated graphics card in a PCIe slot.
Why plugging into the motherboard can hurt gaming performance
Integrated graphics are suitable for basic tasks and less demanding games, but typically cannot compete with your dedicated graphics card — even if you know how to boost GPU performance without buying new hardware. If Windows runs your game on integrated graphics instead, you're missing out on the performance of your dedicated GPU.
Plugging into the motherboard doesn't always leave the dedicated GPU idle. In some Windows configurations, that card can still render games and pass the frames through integrated graphics, potentially adding overhead. Microsoft doesn't state a percentage of performance loss for this configuration, and the impact will depend on the hardware. That's why some gamers don't notice the mistake immediately.
For others, it's a black screen. Motherboard video outputs won't work with Intel desktop processors carrying an F or KF suffix, since those chips lack integrated graphics. Some PCs also disable the integrated GPU when a dedicated card is installed, so a blank screen doesn't necessarily mean your graphics card has failed.
How to make sure you're using the right port
Luckily, the correct ports are typically easy to find. The motherboard's video outputs are grouped with its USB, Ethernet and audio ports. The graphics card has its own outputs on a separate expansion bracket, typically lower down on the back of a conventional tower. They're often horizontal rather than vertical, but orientation isn't universal, so check which ports belong to the graphics card.
Turn off the PC, move the monitor cable to the graphics card and select the corresponding input on the monitor. Both HDMI and DisplayPort support high-refresh-rate gaming, provided your graphics card, monitor and cable support the resolution and refresh rate you want. DisplayPort comes standard on most modern gaming monitors, but if you are already using HDMI and it is working at the resolution and refresh rate you need, then you don't need to purchase a new cable. For Windows 11, go to Settings > System > Display > Advanced display and check the refresh rate.
Do remember, though, that a 100Hz monitor that's set to 60Hz will only show 60 updates per second, no matter what the graphics card renders. If your screen goes black after switching to the graphics card, try a different GPU port or cable. Before checking the power connectors or seating on the card, shut down and unplug the PC. Finally, if integrated graphics aren't disabled, you can even connect a second monitor to the motherboard's output, depending on your system's compatibility.

Vallari Sheel wishes she could carry a camera or a pair of binoculars without being asked what her father does for a living. Once, looking at a tree in her south Delhi neighbourhood, about 50 metres away from her home, a man in a car screamed at her: “You have been clicking photos here for 10 days. What are you going to do with them?”
Sheel, an urban ecologist, spends hours observing trees of all types in all seasons. She often travels by car for her own safety, worries about the impact of her work on her family, and has clear guidance for her female interns when they are, inevitably, approached: don’t engage, don’t respond.
“It’s the men who ask such intrusive questions: Who are you? Where are you from? What does your father do?” she says.
Sheel was recounting these experiences atop Delhi’s oldest fort inside Sanjay Van, a sprawling city forest overlooking a 12th-century minaret. She was one of about 20 women who had gathered on a crisp Sunday morning in October to enjoy nature, safely. Many had never experienced a forest before.
Among the group were a scientist who had stopped birding since she moved to Delhi, a psychiatrist who can’t find a safe place to run, and an environmental planner who cycles everywhere. For many women, simple pleasures such as enjoying nature have become beset by gender crimes.
“The city feels designed to crush any form of freedom, any form of exploration,” says Neha Sinha, who organised the walk. Author of My Wild City: Finding Nature, Meaning, and Hope in India’s Capital, Sinha has been organising these walks for two years.
During her own walks around the city’s forts, forests and wetlands to observe the diminishing number of fireflies, flying foxes, howling jackals, leopards and hyenas, civets and owls, and groves of 350-year-old trees, she has faced the wrath of men. She has changed her route countless times to mislead stalkers, and been asked by men on the street how much she would charge for sex.
“As has everybody else,” she says. “Nearly every woman I know has called a cop saying ‘I have a stalker.’ In a culture that tells you not to go out … how do you make nature your own?”
Two weeks before the women gathered on the walking trails of Sanjay Van, dotted with ruellias, vajradantis and jaal trees, hundreds of people had joined a protest in Delhi over the gang-rape of a 17-year-old in a public park.
Their demand was to make public spaces safer for women. The government’s response was to ban entry to public parks after sunset.
For Alankrita Narayan, a wildlife conservation student who often needs to work alone at night, that rule was unhelpful. During an internship, she recalls, her organisation trained her for worst-case scenarios in the jungle: What if something happens to your partner? What if you encounter a man carrying a weapon? What if you encounter a forest officer asking for sexual favours?
“And I was like, where did the animal come in here? What if I’m caught alone and a leopard comes in front of me? And they were like, ‘Oh, don’t worry about the leopard. It’s a man you don’t want to run into,” she says. Sinha agrees: “Animals have rules.”
Paroma Mukherjee, a photographer, recalls the advice she once got from a well-known photographer: be inconspicuous, wear clothes that blend in, keep your equipment small. “But then, he was a man. So he could blend in,” she adds.
“Men can pee on the road and we can’t even carry a camera,” another woman says. “You know, we had to take a detour today to avoid a lonely stretch on our way here,” says another. “I carry a pepper spray,” another adds.
On group walks, the women pick up and drop off each other at their homes, wait outside the forest gate until everyone has arrived, and stick together in isolated areas. “I always tell women, ‘Don’t go alone’,” Sinha says.
“We started the walk at 7am today, which is late for birdwatching, but everybody could not leave home while it was still dark,” she says.
However, the group agree that many of these measures might not work for women from less privileged backgrounds, who then miss out.
“No woman in the city is fully free,” Sinha says.
Walking as a woman is an act of resistance, as is observing nature. “Because you’re actually slowing down when you do that,” she says. “It’s so different from the instant gratification culture that we have today. It is more of an immersion, rather than conquering. Both are very political acts.”
In the heart of New Delhi, where India’s senior officials and dignitaries live, there are thousands of fruit bats that swarm out of their roosts every evening to feast on mahua trees.
“And on very clear wintry nights, when everything is silent, I even hear jackals crying and laughing from my home. It’s almost like a parallel city,” Sinha says.
Over three hours, the women collect cuttings, peer and marvel at speckle-like flowers through a pocket microscope, discuss the colonial concepts of wild plants labelled as weeds, chat about the drongo, black kite and tailorbird they spotted, and the next walk.
“Can we do it at night?” someone asks. “What would the forest look like at night?”
Sinha describes a previous night walk experience when frogs had put up an orchestral noise, fireflies lit the bushes and jackals were laughing. “It was the most eerie, magical, bewitching atmosphere I have ever experienced,” she says.
Men, she points out, can simply go ahead and enjoy such experiences, but women have to create an ecosystem around them to be able to.
But, she promises her enthusiastic group, she will try to arrange a night walk.

New Indian mega library rocked by scandal over 'AI-generated books'
- Published
An Indian court has ordered an investigation into allegations that a public library in the southern state of Tamil Nadu bought hundreds of books suspected of being generated using AI.
The controversy began after Tamil novelist Perumal Murugan raised concerns about books containing false information and questionable authorship at a newly opened library in Coimbatore city.
The Madras High Court has ordered the state's anti-corruption agency to investigate the purchases and freeze bank accounts linked to a publisher accused of supplying the books.
The state government has blamed the previous Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party-led administration for buying the books. The DMK denies allegations.
Tamil Nadu's School Education Minister A Rajmohan has described the allegations as potentially "India's first AI scam" and said the investigation would cover purchases at other public libraries across the state.
The case has raised wider questions about the growing use of AI in publishing, where tools can generate entire books quickly and cheaply, but also produce false information and invented references.
It has also highlighted the challenges facing libraries and publishers in checking the authenticity of books as AI-generated content becomes more widespread.
The controversy centres on the Periyar Arivulagam library, built at a cost of about 3bn rupees ($34m; £26m). Named after social reformer Periyar EV Ramasamy, it was inaugurated on 16 October by Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay.
Murugan, whose novels Pyre and One Part Woman have received international recognition, raised concerns after visiting the library last month.
Writing in an online magazine, he alleged that nearly 1,800 books in its Tamil section had been supplied by a little-known publisher called Agal Vilakku Pathippagam.
He said many of the books carried unfamiliar authors' names, unusually high prices and questionable International Standard Book Numbers (ISBNs).
One book cited in the controversy, Naladiyar Vaazhvin Vazhikatti (A Guide to Life through Naladiyar), was reportedly priced at 1,445 rupees for 300 pages.
It describes Naladiyar as a Tamil poet and philosopher, although Naladiyar is a classical Tamil work consisting of 400 four-line verses on morality and ethics.
Another book reportedly attributes the ancient Tamil poem Madurai Kanchi to an incorrect author. It remains unclear whether AI was used to produce any of the disputed books.
Questions have also been raised about a book found at another public library in Madurai which names renowned economist Jean Drèze as its author.
The book, Democracy and People's Rights in the Contemporary World, names renowned economist Jean Drèze as its author and was published by Phoenix Publishing House.
Drèze did not respond to BBC Tamil's request for comment but told The Hindu newspaper earlier this week that he had not written the book, raising concerns that his name may have been used without his permission.
BBC Tamil visited a Chennai address listed by Agal Vilakku and another publisher named in the controversy, Phoenix Publishing House, but found no signs identifying either business.
A woman at the address confirmed that Agal Vilakku operated there. Its proprietor, Mohan, declined to comment, saying the matter was before the courts.
The controversy has prompted writers, academics and publishers to question how the books were selected for public libraries.
More than 160 writers, researchers, artists and publishers have signed a joint statement calling for an independent inquiry, the release of procurement records and an audit of library collections across Tamil Nadu.
They have also called for the recovery of public money if the investigation finds that funds were misused.
The group questioned how the disputed books could have passed through a selection process involving expert committees, price negotiations and several levels of review.
The state government has ordered an internal audit of public library collections.
Rajmohan said 523 books had already been removed from the historic Connemara Public Library in Chennai city after preliminary checks raised concerns about their authenticity and quality.
Disputed books have also been removed from Periyar Arivulagam, while anti-corruption officials examine procurement records and inspect other libraries, he added.
The controversy also sparked a political row in Tamil Nadu. Rajmohan accused the previous DMK government of ordering the disputed books and said the state would seek to recover public money if the investigation found wrongdoing.
The DMK has rejected the allegations as politically motivated and has called for an investigation into the purchases.

In his post, Singh also attached a link to the original YouTube interview from which the visuals were taken. Alt News examined the original video uploaded on The Wire’s official YouTube channel in March 2025.
Comparing the viral clip with the March 2025 interview confirms that the visual frames, including Singh’s attire, the background setting, and lighting, are identical. However, the audio track in the viral clip has been changed using AI.
In the original interview, Singh makes no mention of Kulgam, Pulwama, Balakot, or any ‘false flag operations’. Instead, he is heard discussing civil-military relations and institutional oversight.
To sum up, a manipulated video of journalist and strategic affairs analyst Sushant Singh is circulating on social media with users misidentifying him as journalist and FORCE editor Pravin Sawhney. The claim that the speaker in the video termed India’s counter-terrorism measures in Kulgam and Pulwama ‘false flag operations’ is false as well.

An iOS update did include a "Remote Control" feature that appeared to be enabled automatically.
The feature was introduced as part of the iOS 26 update, not iOS 27, and it does not allow users to remotely access a phone's "activity." Rather, it expands the functionality of the previously existing "Live Listen" accessibility feature. It is only functional on devices signed into the same Apple account, and it requires a user to intentionally initiate a Live Listen session on that device.
A rumor has circulated online since October that Apple released an update automatically enabling an option for outsiders to remotely access a phone's activity.
The claim spread on social media platforms such as Facebook (archived) and Instagram (archived). Many of the posts offered warnings about the feature and instructions on how to turn it off, like this one (archived) from a Facebook user:
If you have an iPhone and installed the iOS 27 update, you might not know that Apple turned ON the option for someone to remotely access your activity on your phone.
In short, Apple did put out a "Remote Control" feature in an update, but not iOS 27, as posts claimed. According to their Settings app, the feature released in iOS 26, and the assertion that the feature allowed "someone to remotely access" activity on users' phones was overstated. As such, we have rated this claim as mostly false.
(Screenshot from iPhone/Snopes illustration)
We reached out to Apple for more information about the "Remote Control" feature and to ask whether the iOS 26 update automatically enabled it across all devices. We will update the story if we receive a response.
According to the Apple Support website, Live Listen allows an iPhone to "act like a microphone," allowing users to "hear a conversation in a noisy area or even hear someone speaking across the room." It was originally intended to work with hearing aids, but was expanded in iOS 12 to include AirPods or Beats earphones.
The iOS 26 "Remote Control" setting added new functionality to the feature, allowing Apple devices like iPads and Apple Watches to view and control Live Listen sessions, as long as they are nearby and signed into the same Apple Account.
For example, a student in the back of a noisy lecture hall could put their phone next to their professor at the start of class and remotely control a Live Listen session from their iPad signed into the same Apple account, allowing them to pause, resume and view a transcript of the picked-up audio without getting up from their seat.
Live Listen is situated within the "Accessibility" menu, indicating that Apple intended the feature especially for those with hearing-related difficulties.
(Screenshot from iPhone)
Remote control of a user's Live Listen session can only take place if that user intentionally started the session, and it only provides access to a transcript of audio near the user's iPhone. A bad actor who gained access to a device signed into a user's Apple account wouldn't be able to start a Live Listen session on that user's device using "Remote Control" — that user would have to be the one to start the session. Because of this, there is little risk of someone using the feature nefariously.
Based on user testimony and our own testing, the feature did appear to be automatically enabled as of the iOS 26 update. However, official Apple developer notes (archived) for the update made no mention of the terms "Remote Control" or "Live Listen."
For further reading, Snopes investigated the extent to which incognito mode protects users' data, and found it might be less than most users expected.

LED lights have become an everyday reality in homes, offices, public places and significantly, our screens. And while their energy efficiency is welcome, for many people, their increased use has led to eye discomfort: this includes sleep issues, a blinding sensation while driving at night, redness and watering. Ophthalmologists say this problem is on the rise and point to multiple factors behind it, including brightness levels, positioning of the light, its temperature, colour-tone, and flickering effects.
Apart from lighting up our homes and workplaces, LED lights are now in every gadget, including mobile phones, laptops as well as television sets. Constant exposure can cause mild to extreme visual discomfort, glare, eye strain, and even headaches for some people. This is a genuine visual concern experienced by many people, says Sugato Paul, consultant, ophthalmology at Manipal Hospital, Broadway, Kolkata. Dr Paul explains that discomfort is primarily associated with high luminance and excessive brightness. “Many cool-white LEDs have a relatively higher proportion of short-wavelength (blue) light, generally in the 400–500 nm range. This can increase the perception of brightness, contribute to visual discomfort and make certain individuals more susceptible to glare under specific circumstances,” he says.

New Delhi, Nov 14: Congress leader and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Saturday alleged that democracy in India was destroyed in 2014, accusing the BJP-led government of compromising electoral and democratic institutions to retain power. Addressing an event in Hyderabad, Rahul Gandhi questioned the legitimacy of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, claiming that 140 million voters who participated in the polls had subsequently been declared non-existent or non-voters.
“If the Election Commission has declared 140 million voters illegal non-voters, then how is that election possibly legitimate?” he asked, according to The Week. Citing Maharashtra, Rahul Gandhi alleged that seven million new voters were added to the electoral rolls within three months and all of them voted for the BJP, helping the party win the Assembly elections despite his alliance securing a similar vote share in the Lok Sabha polls.
He alleged that India’s electoral system underwent a fundamental change in 2014 with the infusion of huge amounts of money into politics. “We discovered it, and we have proven it without any doubt is that democracy was destroyed in India in 2014,” he said aas reported by regional media.
Rahul Gandhi also alleged a nexus between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and industrialist Gautam Adani, claiming that the distinction between business and politics had disappeared. Sheikh Hasina is “confident” she will return to Bangladesh in December, according to exiled members of her party, after the disgraced former prime minister applied for a new passport this week.
Hasina has been living in self-imposed exile since August 2024 when she was toppled from power by a mass uprising against her authoritarian rule. She crossed the border to India, where she has since been allowed to live freely in Delhi.
Last November, a tribunal in Bangladesh found Hasina guilty of crimes against humanity and sentenced her to death over her crackdown on a student uprising that left an estimated 1,400 people dead.
Her return to Bangladesh is likely to be disruptive for the country where Hasina’s party, Awami League, is still banned and thousands of its members are in jail. Should she be allowed to return, she is likely to be arrested immediately.
Hasina first raised the prospect of going back to Bangladesh in August. Speaking to the Guardian this week, several exiled Awami League leaders also living in India confirmed that Hasina was serious and “confident” about returning by next month. They confirmed that several other party figures had already returned in anticipation.
On Monday, a British lawyer acting on behalf of Hasina wrote to the Bangladesh high commission in Delhi requesting a new passport and national identity card to be issued “in a timely fashion”, in a letter seen by the Guardian.
“The reason our leader Sheikh Hasina has applied for a passport is that she genuinely wants to return,” said a party leader based in the Indian city of Kolkata, who spoke on condition of anonymity because he is not authorised to speak to the media on the party’s behalf.
Hasina has rejected the charges against her and claimed the tribunal that convicted her was illegitimate. “She is confident about her return, which is why she has applied for a new passport and a national identity card. If the authorities do not issue her a passport, she will apply for a travel pass to make her return to Bangladesh possible,” said the Awami League leader.
Since Hasina’s conviction, the Bangladesh government has put pressure on the Indian authorities to extradite the former prime minister. However, the Indian government, which was close to Hasina while she was in power, has ignored the demands, straining ties between the two countries.
This week, the Bangladesh government said that, as a “terrorist”, Hasina would only be allowed to return via an “acceptable prisoner exchange” under the India-Bangladesh extradition treaty.
Aminul Islam, the chief prosecutor of the tribunal that sentenced Hasina, said there was “no legal scope” for her to be issued a new passport as she was a “convicted fugitive”.
Islam emphasised that Hasina would be hanged if she returned, as the deadline for her to appeal against her conviction had passed. “Sheikh Hasina has no option but to face the execution of the verdict,” he said.
Despite the abuses and oppression that mired her 15 years in power and subsequent conviction for crimes against humanity, Hasina still commands significant popularity among the thousands of Awami League cadre still in Bangladesh, many of whom have been driven underground.
Analysts said they believed her decision to return was driven by an attempt to revive her support base and destabilise the newly elected government, led by Tarique Rahman. It came to power in February during Bangladesh’s first democratic election in decades.
The government has since struggled with inflation and protests that shut down garment factories, which the Awami League hopes to use to its advantage.
Another Awami League leader said all those in exile intended to follow Hasina back to Bangladesh, despite many of them facing serious criminal charges and having been given lengthy prison sentences in absentia.
“Some of us have been sentenced in absentia by kangaroo courts, and we know we will be jailed. But we are ready to face the consequences and return to our own people. We will fight this politically,” said the senior leader, who is based in India.
Some senior party figures have returned in recent months, including the former MP Mustaque Ahmed Ruhi. He was immediately arrested on his return in September and faces prosecution over an alleged murder during the 2024 uprising.
Exiled Awami League leaders have continued to meet in Kolkata, where many of them are living, and are routinely summoned to Delhi to meet Hasina.
Speaking over email this week, Hasina told the Associated Press: “If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people.”

Trump team mulling Howard Lutnick’s future as commerce secretary after Nvidia scandal, report says
Criticism of Lutnick's actions predates Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s Thursday resignation

Senior White House officials are debating whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick should be removed from office after an espionage scandal involving Nvidia's now-former chief executive Jensen Huang, two sources told Reuters.
Lutnick has faced intensifying scrutiny from lawmakers over the Trump administration's reluctance to place dozens of Chinese firms on a US trade blacklist, as well as questions regarding government oversight of Nvidia's exports to China.
Concerns regarding Lutnick's conduct surfaced before Huang announced his departure on Thursday. The chief executive of the prominent AI semiconductor manufacturer resigned following reports of an affair with Alice Huang, a figure suspected by US agencies of espionage for Beijing.
Criticism of Lutnick's failure to curb AI chip transfers to China has intensified alongside the expanding fallout of Jensen Huang's actions.
Neither the White House nor the Commerce Department answered Reuters’ requests for comment on the new claims surrounding Lutnick's position. Earlier Thursday, a White House spokesperson said President Donald Trump "maintains complete confidence in the secretary and his ability to carry out the position."
In June, Reuters revealed that the Trump administration refrained from placing Chinese AI startup DeepSeek, memory manufacturer CXMT, and over 100 additional firms flagged as national security risks onto a trade blacklist.
No updates have been added to that list since October 2025, marking the longest gap without additions in over a decade. Previous reports indicated the US Commerce Department refrained from listing further Chinese enterprises out of concern over escalating tensions between the United States and China.
"Secretary Howard Lutnick and Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler must explain why they have not closed export control loopholes and act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China’s military," said Sen. Elizabeth Warren, a Democrat representing Massachusetts.
Warren, who is set to lead the Senate Banking Committee starting in January, and incoming Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chair Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat, wrote to Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, telling the administration to preserve all documents related to Nvidia’s exports of advanced AI chips to China and related national security risks.
Nvidia sales questioned
The senators cited allegations surrounding Jensen Huang's personal relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which has purchased more than $4.8 billion worth of advanced Nvidia AI chips since June 2024.
Democrats US Sen. Ron Wyden of Oregon and Rep. Richard Neal of Massachusetts, top figures on the Senate Finance and House Ways and Means committees respectively, sent a letter to Lutnick Thursday detailing their inquiry into approvals allowing Nvidia AI chip sales to Chinese firms "with concerning links to the Chinese government, military, and sanctioned entities."
The legislators further challenged Trump's decision authorizing Nvidia to ship advanced H200 AI processors to China in December 2025 in exchange for a portion of export revenues collected via Commerce Department actions, which they described as "an unconstitutional export tax."
Jensen Huang consistently advocated for expanding exports to China, resisting sustained pressure from national security hawks in both parties seeking tighter restrictions on Beijing's tech access.
Nvidia's statement announcing Jensen Huang's resignation did not address his actions.
Florida Republican Rep. Brian Mast argued that Congress needs to scrutinize the Commerce Department's procedure for approving chip sales, though he noted he retains confidence in Lutnick.
Louisiana Republican Sen. John Kennedy told Politico that Lutnick needs to address questions regarding the authorization of advanced American semiconductor exports to China.
Lutnick, a former Wall Street executive who co-chaired Trump's transition effort, shares a 30-year friendship with Trump and appeared in 2008 as a guest on The Apprentice, the TV reality program hosted by Trump.
Axios reported Wednesday that Lutnick stalled measures proposed by Trump to crack down on firms suspected of rerouting Nvidia chips to China.
Arkansas US Sen. Tom Cotton, the Republican chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, urged Lutnick on Thursday to ban CXMT 688825.SS from operating in the US and block its access to American tech.
CXMT did not respond to Reuters’ request for comment.
